channel.title: The Cross Section
channel.description: An AI-powered digest and trend analysis of hep-ex and hep-ph

item.title: Monday, November 2, 2026
item.description:
Quad lenses lean toward core collapse

Gilman et al. arXiv:2610.40766 analyze 29 quadruply imaged quasars and find halo densities consistent with gravothermal core collapse. They interpret this as elastic Yukawa SIDM and apply cluster and satellite-evaporation limits. The favored region is 20–80 GeV dark matter with MeV mediators and σ/m∼10²–10⁴ cm²/g at 10 km/s. Mediator bounds then push them toward an invisibly decaying neutrinophilic scalar. This is the third result in two weeks pointing away from CDM-density subhalos. Zhang et al. found none of 5000+ CDM subhalos dense enough, and Tekverk et al. found SIDM matches three known perturbers far more often. The new paper is a population statement, not a per-perturber one, though the authors still say “hints.” Elsewhere, an extra loop order excludes a minimal SUSY GUT, and phase-transition GW predictions shed three idealizations. The 248 keV LZ event drew no papers.

Themes

Phase transitions, less idealized

Three papers each relax a standard assumption: - Cutrona et al. arXiv:2610.40775 find that gravity, through non-minimal couplings, can enlarge or shrink the parameter space where supercooled radiative-symmetry-breaking transitions complete. - Finetti et al. arXiv:2610.40781 let dark-sector sound waves leak into the visible fluid. The total GW signal is generally suppressed and its spectral shape changes. - Blum et al. arXiv:2610.41504 show nucleated bubbles are not spherical, with δR/R∼(ħ/S_b)¹/2≈0.1 for typical cosmological transitions.

This is in the spirit of last week’s error-budget thread, now applied to GW forecasts.

Loop order decides

Allwicher et al. arXiv:2610.40821 find that Tera-Z gauge-coupling precision becomes sensitive to higher-loop running all the way up. In minimal SU(5) with proton-decay limits, two loops point to PeV-scale SUSY, while three loops appear to exclude the model.

Adelaja et al. arXiv:2610.40823 propose a retained signature-changing soft-gluon term as the source of the unexplained non-planar ζ_2 violations at small x. Those violations appear in the three- and four-loop non-singlet splitting functions, which were September’s headline. The proposal reproduces both with no tuned coefficient and predicts five-loop terms.

Bera et al. arXiv:2610.42062 complete the leading-colour two-loop integrals for tt̅γ, including elliptic entries. That follows last week’s genus-two tt̅ amplitudes.

Structure over size

Alison et al.’s CoReNet arXiv:2610.40749 builds the decay chain into the architecture. With 1508 parameters it matches a transformer more than 100× larger in HH→4b, extending last week’s tagger-compression run. Hart et al.’s REM arXiv:2610.41889 goes from hits to particles to resonances in full simulation, beating ML particle flow. Chung arXiv:2610.41894 asks the information-theoretic version of the question for calorimeters.

Neutrino generators, rebuilt

Graham-Jones et al. arXiv:2610.40866 put a consistent chiral EFT with Δ(1232) pion production into Sherpa, going through FeynRules and UFO. Prasad et al. arXiv:2610.40912 decompose a DNN’s inclusive electron–carbon prediction into exclusive generator channels by reweighting.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.40766: A 29-lens population pointing at core collapse, with a concrete particle model attached. It is the strongest entry yet in the SIDM-vs-CDM lensing thread.
  • arXiv:2610.40821: The two-loop vs three-loop flip on minimal SUSY SU(5) is a sharp result. The “IR determination” of the colour-triplet mass explains why.
  • arXiv:2610.41894: Treats hadronic resolution as an information ladder. On the same Geant4 events, the full record reaches 1.29% vs 2.14% at 20 GeV, and each readout dimension gets a measured value.
  • arXiv:2610.40749: Already used in several CMS searches. It recovers truth jet pairings without ever being trained on them.
  • arXiv:2610.42143: Kats makes a first strange-quark polarimetry measurement via Λ in W→cs̅, on CMS Open Data. The result is consistent with zero for now; the method and projections are the point.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.40724 Nuclear-geometry-tagging events in high-energy Ne–Ne collisions — Joachim Carlo Kristian Bjerg Hansen et al. (nucl-th). In Glauber simulations, tip–tip ²⁰Ne configurations can be selected at ~0.55 purity, as the small-system program moves past oxygen.
  • arXiv:2610.40911 Search for long-lived heavy neutral leptons… — CMS Collaboration (hep-ex). Muon-system displaced vertices extend HNL reach to 2–4 GeV at mixings of 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵. No excess.
  • arXiv:2610.40967 Separating Fermion and Gauge Resonances with Species-Dependent Lightcones in Warped Geometry — Lisa Randall et al. (hep-ph). Fermion partners at 6.6–12 TeV coexist with 30 TeV KK gluons.
  • arXiv:2610.40793 Layered Wire-Grid Haloscope for Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark Photons — Andrea Caputo (hep-ph). Projected axion reach below CAST up to 1.4 meV.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.40766 — Hints of self-interacting dark matter from strong gravitational lensing (Daniel Gilman et al.)

What they did. This is a recast, not new data. It takes the G26 likelihood on median core-collapse times in two halo-mass bins, 10⁶–10⁸ and 10⁸–10¹⁰.7 M_⊙, from 29 JWST quads. G26 disfavors CDM with Bayes factors of 8:1 to 24:1. The authors map that likelihood onto elastic Yukawa SIDM using the Gurian et al. gravothermal t_c, which is valid across Knudsen regimes. They then multiply in cluster (<0.1 cm²/g at 1500 km/s), satellite-evaporation (<10 cm²/g at 250 km/s) and relic-density likelihoods.

The likelihood peaks at σ_10≈1000 or 200 cm²/g, depending on the subhalo-modeling weights. Both peaks sit at α_χ∼10⁻³.5–10⁻³ and m_χ/m_ϕ>10³.5. At α_χ=10⁻³ the viable region is m_χ∼20–80 GeV with m_ϕ<20 MeV, much of it near the s-wave resonances. To survive mediator bounds, they adopt Dirac DM with a complex scalar dilepton that decays to ν_Rν_R; lepton charge forbids tree-level Higgs mixing. Kinetic decoupling at ∼0.14 MeV clears the ≳7 keV requirement. ΔN_eff can stay below 0.107, but only with extra entropy release or a tuned Higgs-portal history.

Why it matters. The paper turns the lensing thread into a concrete particle-physics target with N_eff and direct-detection handles. It also shows that elastic scattering cannot collapse standard field halos faster than 2.0 Gyr and 2.9 Gyr in the two mass bins. Shorter collapse times would point to inelastic or dissipative physics instead.

Caveats. CDM is not formally excluded. The result depends on the assumed tidal acceleration (3–5×), subhalo abundance, and collapsed-profile slope. The relic relation carries a factor-of-5 allowance because the bound-state-formation calculation does not yet exist. If mergers delay collapse, the inferred long-mean-free-path cross sections are only lower bounds.

arXiv:2610.40821 — The Yottascale at Tera-Z: Petascale SUSY? (Lukas Allwicher et al.)

What they did. Gauge couplings are run from m_Z to the GUT scale at successive loop orders and compared against current and FCC-ee input errors; δα_s drops from 9×10⁻⁴ to 10⁻⁴. In the SM, 2-loop running is already only marginally adequate, and FCC-ee precision would resolve 4-loop effects. In the CMSSM, the 2-loop SUSY threshold shift to α_3 makes unification worse at three loops: ξ̅ goes from 0.1–5% to about 2.4%.

In minimal SUSY SU(5), the 1-loop GUT matching fixes M_H_c independently of α_5. The reason is group-theoretic: X and Σ together fill a complete 24. The same holds in Georgi–Glashow, but fails for multi-field breaking sectors.

This makes M_H_c purely IR-determined and loop-order sensitive. With τ/τ_SK≃1.55×10⁻⁴⁽M_H_c/YeV)²⁽m_S/PeV)², the two loop orders give opposite answers: - Two loops: M_H_c grows with m_S, so the Super-K K⁺ν̅ bound is evaded near PeV. - Three loops: M_H_c falls with m_S and stays excluded at every SUSY scale, including against Hyper-K projections.

Why it matters. It is a clean example of perturbative order, rather than data, flipping a model’s viability. It also gives a concrete theory requirement for Tera-Z.

Caveats. The 2-loop GUT thresholds are unknown, and the authors admit they could cancel the effect if comparable in size. Results above m_S∼100 TeV are extrapolated with analytic degenerate-spectrum thresholds. The analysis does not cover split SUSY or gravity-induced operators.

arXiv:2610.41894 — Calorimetry as inference: the information content of particle showers (Wonyong Chung)

What they did. The paper casts calorimetry as Fisher/Bayes estimation on a lattice of records. It proves monotonicity under refinement, exact information scaling under Poisson thinning, and a 1/(1+cv²⁾ clustering cost. It also shows that the a/√(E)⊕b budget is the Gaussian-equality case of a two-sided bound.

It then measures a resolution ladder with trained estimators (validated to ≤0.34% against exact posteriors on solvable cascades). The data are Geant4 11.4.2 FTFP_BERT π⁻ events in a large Cu block, with the neutron tracking cut removed. At 20 GeV the ladder reads:

Record σ/E
Sum 4.07%
+ S,C 2.16%
+ longitudinal shape 1.60%
+ time 1.32%
+ counts 1.29%

The full record is about 5.5%/√(E)⊕0.3% over 20–100 GeV. That is a factor 1.7–1.9 below the Lee–Livan–Wigmans one-functional construction evaluated on the same events (2.14%; 2.7% as published).

What the readout dimensions are worth: - Shape: radial information is worth only 2–3%; depth sampling saturates at about 1 λ_I. - Time: a 10 ns gate costs about a third in resolution. - Floor: in-volume neutrinos from stopped-μ chains leave an estimated 0.99% floor, barely reduced from their 1.12% marginal. This argues for muon-stop tagging.

Caveats. All records are truth-level, single-particle and pileup-free. The count-based record elements have no hardware counterpart, so 1.60% is the hardware-relevant number. Cross-run spreads reach 0.19% at 20 GeV. Model dependence is real: - Transferring FTFP_BERT-trained estimators to QGSP_BERT events shifts the full record by +19% (no retraining was done for QGSP_BERT). - Retraining with high-precision neutron transport leaves the top value nearly unchanged (1.30%) but cuts the time increment from 0.28% to 0.17%.

item.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
item.description:
φ flows like a meson

ALICE arXiv:2610.36237 reports the first φ elliptic flow measured in a small system. In central and semi-central O–O collisions at 5.36 TeV they see mass ordering at low p_T and a 10σ baryon–meson splitting above 3 GeV. The φ has nearly the Λ’s mass, yet its v_2 tracks the K⁰_S, not the Λ. That disfavors a purely mass-driven pattern and points to recombination from a flowing partonic medium. It is a sharper discriminant than CMS’s O–O baryon-to-meson enhancement (arXiv:2608.18256), which anchored the year’s small-system thread. The day’s other hard number is CONUS+ at 10.2σ. The rest of the listing is mostly methods, and the 248 keV LZ event drew no new papers today.

Themes

Small systems, partonic

Beyond the φ result, Mallick et al. arXiv:2610.36922 validate a nonflow subtraction for symmetry-plane correlators and symmetric cumulants. They test it on Angantyr, where flow is absent by construction, before predicting O–O. That is the control these multiparticle observables need at low multiplicity. In Pb–Pb, ALICE arXiv:2610.36307 finds the antideuteron–net-Λ correlation matches Thermal-FIST. The earlier antideuteron–antiproton discrepancy therefore looks like a nucleosynthesis effect, not a hadronization one. Together with yesterday’s first O–O I_AA, oxygen is now producing discriminating measurements, not just existence proofs.

Fits, faster and more honest

  • Fitters. Elmarassy et al. arXiv:2610.35927 benchmark minimizers and find BFGS variants consistently about 10× faster than Migrad at equal precision.
  • PDF training dynamics. Chiefa et al. arXiv:2610.36034 extend NTK gradient-flow analysis to a multi-flavour DIS fit. A few leading modes carry the PDFs, and the data noise sits in the late-learned modes. This complements Elmer et al.’s NTK calibration study from 10-23.
  • Generative models and nPDFs. Badaracco et al.’s SIGMA arXiv:2610.37398 profiles generative-model fit uncertainty inside the goodness-of-fit test. Derakhshanian arXiv:2610.37254 finds secondary minima in lead nPDFs that the Hessian method misses.

This is the week’s error-budget thread, moved from physics inputs to the statistical machinery itself.

Reactor CEvNS goes precision

Ackermann et al. (CONUS+) arXiv:2610.37318, with the companion analysis arXiv:2610.37345, count 1555 ± 152 events. That is N_s/N_SM=0.91±0.14, with thresholds of 140–170 eV_ee. Their sin²θ_W=0.225±0.022 at ~10 MeV is a single-experiment point. It sits beside last week’s combined CEνNS+ν–e value of 0.233⁺⁰.007_-0.006.

Taggers under the microscope

Rai et al. arXiv:2610.37137 use model stitching to show the primary Lund plane’s deficit relative to ParT is representational, not computational. The deficit is invisible in AUC. Rankin et al.’s SuperJEPA arXiv:2610.36121 finds self-supervision helps even when large labeled samples exist. Wu et al. arXiv:2610.36720 put a full-granularity calorimeter CNN on an FPGA for KOTO, with 99.3% background rejection at 17.9 μs. After the week’s compression results, this is diagnosis rather than shrinkage.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.36237: The φ is the cleanest available test of mass ordering versus recombination, and it comes out on the recombination side.
  • arXiv:2610.37318: The most precise reactor CEνNS measurement to date, from a blind analysis.
  • arXiv:2610.37137: A transferable method for locating where a tagger loses information. The gap sits in 0.6% of background jets.
  • arXiv:2610.35927: Unglamorous, but most analyses run Migrad, and the initial-Hessian finding is directly actionable.
  • arXiv:2610.36065: Fontes et al. find linear IR terms cancel through NNLO in non-Abelian heavy-quark pair production when a short-distance mass is used. It is relevant to the mass-scheme questions behind this month’s top-mass threads.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.36062 Late reheating in the era of precision cosmology — Kensuke Akita et al. (hep-ph). Reheating at ~0.4 MeV lowers the cosmological active-ν mass density by up to 5× at fixed physical masses. That bears on last week’s persistent negative-∑m_ν preference.
  • arXiv:2610.37106 Probing new CP-violating sources in Λ_b→Λ_cℓ⁻ν̅_ℓ — Dong-Hao Li et al. (hep-ph). The baryonic mode reaches Wilson-coefficient combinations that D^* angular distributions cannot.
  • arXiv:2610.37258 Precision measurement of the J/ψ→μ⁺μ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ branching fraction… — BESIII Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). The rate agrees with the SM, and the L_μ-L_τ limits are comparable to Belle II’s below 0.7 GeV.
  • arXiv:2610.36684 Antenna-coupled microstrip summing network for wave-like dark matter searches — Chelsea Bartram et al. (hep-ex). A readout adapted from CMB detectors for multi-wavelength ADMX-VERA cavities at 19–21 GHz.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.36237 — Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of φ, K⁰_S, and Λ elliptic flow (ALICE Collaboration)

What they did. ALICE measured identified-hadron v_2 in ~3×10⁹ O–O events at 5.36 TeV, in 0–10% and 10–40% centrality, using a |Δη|>1.2 gap and a low-multiplicity template fit with a 65–100% reference. Signal v_2 comes from simultaneous fits to the invariant mass and V_2Δ(m).

  • Low p_T (<2.2 GeV). The ordering is v_2(K⁰_S) > v_2(Λ) ≈v_2(ϕ). K⁰_S–Λ separates at >10σ and K⁰_S–φ at >5σ.
  • Above 3 GeV. The pattern flips. Λ exceeds K⁰_S at >10σ and exceeds φ at >5σ. The φ is compatible with the K⁰_S despite its Λ-like mass.
  • Scaling. Constituent-quark scaling holds approximately, with deviations comparable to those seen in Pb–Pb.

Why it matters. The φ separates mass from quark content. That makes it a sharper test than baryon-to-meson yield ratios such as CMS’s O–O enhancement. Mass ordering at low p_T combined with type grouping at intermediate p_T is the full heavy-ion pattern, now seen in a system with well-constrained geometry.

Caveats. - The 10σ figure is the Λ–K⁰_S splitting. The comparison that actually discriminates mass from type, Λ–φ, is “>5σ”. With the forward FT0C centrality estimator it drops to about 4.5σ in 0–10%. - Non-flow subtraction is the largest systematic, up to 9% for the φ, and it grows with p_T, exactly where the splitting is claimed. This is why the nonflow validation work (Mallick et al.) matters. - The interpretation is explicitly “qualitative”. No quantitative model comparison is shown, and hydro-plus-fragmentation is acknowledged to generate some species splitting.

arXiv:2610.37318 — High significance measurement of reactor CEνNS on germanium by CONUS+ (N. Ackermann (CONUS+ Collaboration) et al.)

What they did. Run 2 used two new 2.33 kg active-mass point-contact HPGe diodes plus the original 0.94 kg detector, at 20.7 m from the 3.6 GW_th Leibstadt core. Thresholds were 140–170 eV_ee and the exposure was 1296 kg·d reactor-on. The blind likelihood (spectra hidden below 400 eV_ee) gives:

  • N_s = 1555 ±116 (stat) ±98 (syst), a 10.2σ detection against an expected 10.4σ.
  • N_s/N_SM = 0.91 ±0.14, compared with N_SM = 1701 ±198.
  • sin²θ_W = 0.225 ±0.022 at Q ≈10 MeV, against the SM value of 0.2387. This is the lowest-Q CEνNS determination to date.

Why it matters. This is the largest CEνNS sample so far, with precision comparable to COHERENT’s germanium result. It also disfavors the Dresden-II rate and the non-Lindhard quenching behind it. The ratio, however, is systematics-dominated. The 11.6% prediction uncertainty comes mainly from the energy scale near threshold (8.0%) and the quenching factor (7.5%). Until those improve, the sin²θ_W point is not competitive with the combined CEνNS+ν–e value.

Caveats. - The combined fit has χ²/ndf = 1.37 over 381 dof (p = 7×10⁻⁶), driven by detector C3 and by C6’s reactor-off data. Inflating the variances to restore p>0.1 lowers the significance to 9.3σ. - The background-shape-independent on-minus-off fit gives only 1332 ± 420 events (3.1σ). - Per-detector yields straddle the prediction: C6 gives 731 against 604 expected, and C7 gives 714 against 903. - Four analysis changes were made during unblinding. The authors state these were motivated by checks independent of the signal.

arXiv:2610.37137 — What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis (Saurabh Rai et al.)

What they did. The authors built Lund-ParT, a network architecturally identical to ParT but fed Lund declusterings. They then stitched frozen front and back halves of the two networks together through a single trained 128×128 linear map at the class token. All results use 50% of the top-tagging reference dataset.

  • The gap is representational. Standalone rejection at ε_S = 0.5 is 291 for ParT and 136 for the primary-branch Lund-ParT. ParT’s downstream reading the Lund representation reaches 128–136, while Lund-ParT’s own downstream reaches only 120–134. A stronger reader does not recover the missing performance.
  • AUC hides it. Retained AUC stays within 0.977–1.007 throughout.
  • It is localized. The deficit sits in about 0.6% of ParT-rejected background jets. These have a mean mass of 180 GeV and about 67 constituents, yet fewer primary splittings than typical background (11.3 against 12.6).
  • The full tree repairs most of it. Rebuilding on the full C/A tree raises rejection to 248, closing 72% of the gap.
  • Masking. Dropping 12 secondary nodes costs little (230.6 → 186.5). Dropping 12 primary nodes costs almost everything (230.6 → 9.2). This suggests the secondary nodes aid learnability rather than inference.

Why it matters. The method is transferable for locating where a tagger loses information. It also warns against a “primary branch plus a few secondaries” shortcut. On quark/gluon tagging the primary branch already retains 77.6% of ParT’s rejection, and the full tree reaches about 85% of ParT on both tasks.

Caveats. - Absolute rejections sit far below full-scale values (~2000–5000). - The consumer-asymmetry result has p = 0.062 with five seeds. - The hypergraph check (116 against 112) uses a single seed on 10% of the data. - The “learnability” reading is an interpretation of the masking results, not a direct test.

Full texts for arXiv:2610.35927 and arXiv:2610.36065 were not supplied, so they are not covered here.

item.title: Tuesday, October 27, 2026
item.description:
Relic supernova neutrinos, at 2.6σ

Super-Kamiokande arXiv:2610.35619 reports an indication of ν̅e from the diffuse supernova neutrino background, using 5003 days of data. The best-fit flux is 3.6⁺¹.6-1.5 cm⁻²s⁻¹ above 13.3 MeV, 2.6σ from null, and the significance holds across spectral models. It is not a discovery, but it is the first hint of a signal that has only ever produced limits. LHCb supplies the day’s firmer result: the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ seen in D^*-D⁰, extending the season’s strong spectroscopy run. On the theory side, the weight sits in flavor textures, with three papers deriving Yukawa structure from unification or non-invertible symmetries.

Themes

Textures from new symmetries

Hall et al. arXiv:2610.33152 note that y_τ=y_b and y_μ=3y_s both hold near 10⁶ GeV. They read this as low-scale Pati–Salam with μ→e conversion as the direct test. One of their two theories predicts |V_cb|=0.042±0.002, a number that has to face the month’s inclusive/exclusive |V_cb| split.

Two papers use fusion algebras instead: - Distler et al. arXiv:2610.34720 fit mass textures well, but no algebra they study fits masses and mixings together. - Borah et al. arXiv:2610.35587 get inverted ordering with m_3=0. That lines up with Gluza et al.’s finding last week that most mixing schemes prefer inverted ordering.

LLMs graded on QFT

Liu et al.’s QFT-Bench arXiv:2610.33134 has 75 graduate-to-research-level problems. Frontier models exceed 95%, but their chains of thought often fail to justify the correct answers they reach. Saad’s proton_agent arXiv:2610.33593 routes GUT running and proton decay through a deterministic backend and runs on local open models. Both continue the agentic thread that last week produced FeynFacet’s analytic NLO results.

Inelastic DM beyond xenon

Kim et al.’s dark-Higgs model for both the LZ event and the GCE arXiv:2610.25423, covered on 10-20, reappears in today’s listing. Two papers take inelastic kinematics past the 248 keV event itself: - Amarasinghe arXiv:2610.35789 maps the neutrino fog for inelastic scattering on xenon. In some regions it vanishes entirely; in others its onset jumps discontinuously with mass and splitting. - Chiang et al. arXiv:2610.35620 use NGC 1068 to bound threshold-induced spectral deficits in AGN spikes.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.35619: The improvements are in atmospheric-background rejection and the spectral fit. Check how much each contributes before believing the 2.6σ.
  • arXiv:2610.35239: The known D_s⁺ states fail to describe D⁰K⁺, and adding the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ fixes it at >5σ. Its properties match the ψ(2S)π⁻ measurement, which is a welcome open-charm cross-check of a hidden-charm state.
  • arXiv:2610.33152: A unification scale low enough that upcoming μ→e conversion experiments probe part of it. The measured masses fix the flavor structure.
  • arXiv:2610.33134: The unfaithful-reasoning result matters more than the accuracy number for anyone handing derivations to agents.
  • arXiv:2610.35331: First I_AA in O–O, with away-side suppression weaker than in central Pb–Pb. It adds to the year’s small-system QGP thread, though the authors leave selection biases and cold-nuclear-matter effects open.

From the community

  • arXiv:2610.34061 Remembering Brown-Rho scaling — Su Houng lee (nucl-th). A memoir dedicated to Mannque Rho, revisiting what an often-misread scaling law was meant to say.
  • arXiv:2610.35154 LHμC: A high energy, high luminosity muon-hadron collider at CERN — Krzysztof Piotrzkowski (hep-ex). Reuses LHeC infrastructure to reach μ⁺p collisions at 5.3–7.5 TeV, pitched as a bridge between FCC and muon-collider plans.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.33164 Four-loop MS-pole quark mass relation with two different masses — Matteo Fael et al. (hep-ph). Valid for all mass ratios, and improves 18 of 23 colour structures even in the known limits.
  • arXiv:2610.34325 Near-exact Upper Confidence Limits for Axion Haloscopes — Andrea Gallo Rosso et al. (physics.data-an). A likelihood treatment of adaptive scans gives limits 1.4× stronger in ALPHA projections, with the BPM method reinterpreted as e-values.
  • arXiv:2610.33729 Exploring the Limits: Neutrino Mass and Interacting Dark Sector in the DESI Era — Weiqiang Yang et al. (hep-ph). Dark-sector interactions do not rescue positive ∑m_ν; every dataset combination still prefers negative effective masses.
  • arXiv:2610.34880 Light top-flavoured dark matter in dark SMEFT… — Meng-Chao Gao et al. (hep-ph). Only tree-level operators fit Belle II’s B⁺→K⁺νν̅ excess as DM, and B⁰→K^*0+inv is the main constraint on them.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.35619 — Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (Kamiokande Collaboration et al.)

Super-Kamiokande fits 5003.0 days (Oct 2008–Mar 2026, phases SK-IV through VIII, including the Gd-loaded phases) and finds a DSNB flux of 3.6⁺¹.6_-1.5 cm⁻²s⁻¹ (4.8⁺².2_-2.0 events/yr) for E_ν>13.3 MeV, assuming the Horiuchi+09 6 MeV spectral shape. The background-only hypothesis is disfavored at 2.6σ (one-sided). The Kresse+21 and Ashida+23 shapes give 2.7σ and 2.6σ. The Gd phases alone give 2.2σ and the pure-water phases 1.4σ. The simpler model-independent count over 13.3–31.3 MeV gives only 1.8σ (p = 0.036). The best-fit flux sits at the upper end of the Horiuchi+09 range of 2.1–3.9 cm⁻²s⁻¹.

On the digest’s question of where the gain comes from: - Background rejection. An ML NC classifier raises IBD efficiency from 79% to 89% and halves the residual NCQE fraction from 10% to 5%. - Systematics. A T2K beam sample cuts the NC rate uncertainty from 70% to 45%. The neutron-multiplicity uncertainty falls from 30–40% to 10–30%, and the ⁹Li remaining-rate error from 50% to 30%. - Thresholds. The N_n=1 threshold drops from 15.5 to 11.5 MeV.

The paper says only that the combined effect more than doubles the median discovery potential. The provided text does not split that gain by component.

The key caveat is in Appendix B. With the old N_n≠1 threshold, the pure-water phases show an extra contribution at 15.5–21.5 MeV, comparable to the expected signal. Including it shifts the fitted DSNB rate by about 1σ, which is more than statistics should allow. The collaboration attributes this to mismodeled spallation and raises that threshold to 21.5 MeV, at a 13.9% cost in expected signal. That is conservative, but it also shows the spallation model is not yet under control at the sensitivity now being reached.

arXiv:2610.35239 — Observation of the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ state in B⁰→D^*-D⁰K⁺ decays (LHCb collaboration et al.)

LHCb’s amplitude analysis uses 6912 candidates from 9 fb⁻¹, with about 5% background. A model containing only D⁰K⁺ resonances describes the D⁰K⁺ and D^-K⁺ spectra but misses a dip near 4.4 GeV in m(D^-D⁰⁾ (χ²⁼⁸².1 over 64 Dalitz bins).

Adding the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ with its mass and width fixed gives 2ΔNLL =-43.0, which is 6.2σ statistical and 5.3σ after systematics. The state appears through destructive interference rather than as a peak. Its own fit fraction is (1.3±0.4)%, while its interference with the QMI S-wave is (-6.6±1.3)%. J^P=1⁺ is preferred over the alternatives at more than 5σ.

Other results: - With mass and width free, the fit gives 4424±21⁺¹²_-6 MeV and 145±39±17 MeV. These sit 1.8σ and 0.7σ from the ψ(2S)π values, so “consistent” carries a mild mass pull. - Substituting the T_cc̅1(4200) gives only 3.6σ. With both states included, the 4200 drops to 1.6σ. - The T_cc̅1(3900) and T^*_c̅s̅1(2900) are not significant (fit fractions below 0.24% and 0.32% at 95% CL).

This is the first open-charm decay of the state. The measured width ratio Γ(D^*-D⁰⁾/Γ(ψ(2S)π⁻⁾⁼⁰.96±0.29⁺⁰.22_-0.48⁺⁰.57_-0.30 disfavors dominance of either channel. The authors note that theory predictions for this ratio are lacking.

The main caveat is that the dominant systematic is amplitude modeling. The overlapping D⁰K⁺ 1⁻ wave, which carries about 75% of the fit fractions, is described by splines, with a K-matrix alternative used as the systematic variation. The two diverge in phase above 3 GeV.

arXiv:2610.33152 — A Low Scale for Quark–Lepton Unification (Lawrence J. Hall et al.)

Running the Standard Model Yukawas at two loops, the authors find that y_τ=y_b holds at μ_3=5.20⁺⁰.90_-0.76×10⁵ GeV and y_μ=3y_s at μ_2=7.20⁺³.69_-2.33×10⁵ GeV. The ratio μ_2/μ_3 is stable under three-loop running (1.39 → 1.40). The Georgi–Jarlskog relation y_e=y_d/3 arrives later, at about 3×10⁸ GeV. For contrast, at 2×10¹⁶ GeV the three ratios are off by 30–70%.

A sparse Pati–Salam texture produces all three relations. An SU(4)-singlet bidoublet fills the 12, 21 and 33 entries, and an adjoint fills the 22 entry. However, tree-level vector-leptoquark exchange in K_L→μe requires M_X≳2.5×10⁶ GeV, which is above μ_2,3. That leaves two routes: - Electron mass from elsewhere. The heavier-generation relations then survive at (5–7)×10⁵ GeV, with K→μμ as the leading probe. - Two fixed-parameter theories that keep all three relations: - The “123” theory reaches unification through flavor diagonalization alone, at 4.6⁺¹.2_-0.9×10⁶ GeV. - The “12” theory has symmetric Yukawas and unifies at 1.5⁺⁰.7_-0.5×10⁷ GeV. It predicts |V_cb|=0.042±0.002; the paper compares this only to the PDG value 0.0411±0.0012. It also needs an 11% charged-scalar threshold, a negligible up-sector 2–3 rotation, and sinβ≈0.07–0.17.

The μ→e conversion rate is CR_Al≈2.8×10⁻¹⁷⁽¹⁰⁷ GeV/M_X)⁴. Mu2e and COMET Phase II reach about 8×10⁶ GeV, covering most of the 123 range; Mu2e-II and AMF would cover both theories.

Caveats: - About 75–90% of the variance in the unification scales comes from m_d and m_s. - The leading-order texture predicts |V_us|=0.219 against a measured 0.2243; matching it needs a relative phase of about 92° between the up and down light blocks. - Scalar contributions to μ→e conversion are omitted. - In G_422, nucleon-decay bounds of several 10⁶ GeV can arise, but they depend on assumed Planck-suppressed operator coefficients.

item.title: Monday, October 26, 2026
item.description:
Top pairs reach genus two

Buccioni et al. arXiv:2610.32543 deliver the complete two-loop QCD amplitudes for qq̅ and gg→tt̅ in analytic form. They keep full m_t and N_c dependence and work from 417 master integrals. The function space includes several elliptic curves and a genus-two hyperelliptic curve. The authors say this is the first amplitude where genus-two iterated integrals survive in the four-dimensional finite remainder. They also supply high-precision threshold expansions in a public evaluator. Threshold is where the toponium-vs-continuum argument sits, and Ball et al. showed last week that any excess there is entangled with m_t. Elsewhere, the Galactic Center excess gets its most deflationary reading yet, and the 248 keV LZ event loses another candidate explanation.

Themes

Dark-sector excesses, three verdicts

Sands et al. arXiv:2610.32845 build diffuse emission from MHD Milky Way analogs with time-dependent cosmic-ray transport. The gap between instantaneous and time-averaged emission reaches several times the GCE, and some snapshots resemble it in both spectrum and morphology. Coming after Abazajian’s foreground dependence (10-19) and Kim’s narrow dSph corridor (10-20), this reads the excess as a look-elsewhere fluctuation.

Aristizabal Sierra et al. arXiv:2610.32747 use LZ’s empty recoil region to set new bounds on atmospheric-neutrino up-scattering to sterile fermions above ~50 MeV. Fitting the 248 keV event this way needs couplings at the edge of perturbativity. That echoes September’s exclusion of neutrino-scattering readings.

Pointing the other way, Tekverk et al. arXiv:2610.31881 find SIDM subhalos match all three gravitational-imaging perturbers far more often than CDM subhalos. This quantifies last week’s finding that none of 5000+ CDM subhalos is dense enough.

Transverse spin from several sides

  • Kang et al.’s FeynFacet arXiv:2610.31745 uses AI agents to derive new analytic NLO hard functions for transverse spin transfer.
  • Yang et al. arXiv:2610.32387 show the mass-induced m h_1T/Q transversity term cancels exactly, so inclusive DIS has no net twist-3 transversity.
  • Cao et al. arXiv:2610.32715 propose a fragmentation energy correlator whose transverse-spin dependence probes the chiral-symmetry-breaking scale.
  • Han et al. arXiv:2610.32741 isolate gluon-transversity GPDs in deuteron TCS through their angular dependence.

All of this continues September’s EIC/JLab-facing nucleon-structure push.

Axions back in the cavity

After last week’s off-haloscope proposals, Gao et al. arXiv:2610.31717 return to the cavity. They pre-excite the mode so the signal is linear in g_aγ and claim KSVZ/DFSZ sensitivity with current technology. The case rests on simulations, so check the noise treatment.

Radford et al. arXiv:2610.32091 add axion electrodynamics to OSIRIS. They find the previously proposed co-linear instability disappears under a consistent reduction, while a counter-propagating Floquet branch survives.

Bodeker et al. arXiv:2610.31756 add an 𝒪(√(λ)) soft-scalar correction to the high-temperature topological susceptibility in SU(2).

Nuclear inputs for neutrinos

Lyu et al. arXiv:2610.32947 put chiral three-body currents into shell-model 0νββ matrix elements for the first time, aiming at a truncation-error budget. It is the nuclear-side companion to de Vries’s radiative corrections (10-22). Meng et al. arXiv:2610.32084 predict geoneutrino signals at Jinping using a 0.2° local crust model.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.32543: Genus-two geometry in the finite remainder of a process measured daily. The threshold evaluator is what toponium fits need.
  • arXiv:2610.32845: A physical mechanism, not just another template systematic. If it holds, Fermi-LAT diffuse templates need time dependence.
  • arXiv:2610.31745: Agents doing analytic NLO with gauge, pole and RG checks, plus released code. It is a concrete test case for the AI-theory blueprint from 10-21.
  • arXiv:2610.31881: Per-host matching rates, for example ~0.6 SIDM vs ~0.002 CDM for PJ011646. Simultaneous fits need w≳10² km/s.
  • arXiv:2610.32747: New sterile-fermion bounds from a dark-matter detector, and a clear “not compelling” verdict on the event.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.31759 Discontinuity at the Pole — Dominik Haslehner et al. (hep-th). The vDVZ discontinuity read off pole residues for arbitrary spin: Chebyshev polynomials for massless exchange, Legendre for the massless limit.
  • arXiv:2610.32790 Robustness of the scaled transverse-momentum correlator… — Rutik Manikandhan et al. (hep-ph). With composition fluctuations included, the minimum in the two-component, no-critical-point explanation disappears.
  • arXiv:2610.31761 Prospects of Detecting Cosmological Domain Walls in the CMB — Berkin Gürbüz et al. (astro-ph.CO). Neural ratio estimation reaches roughly the noise floor for η∼10–100 MeV walls.
  • arXiv:2610.31856 Measurements of the neutron background for CURIE — Dakota K. Keblbeck et al. (physics.ins-det). First measured neutron backgrounds at a new 400 m.w.e. site.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.32543 — Analytic two-loop corrections to top-quark pair production at hadron colliders (Federico Buccioni et al.)

Buccioni, Nega, Sauer, Tancredi and Wagner give the complete two-loop qq̅→tt̅ and gg→tt̅ amplitudes in analytic form, with full m_t, N_c, n_l and n_h dependence, through 𝒪(ε²⁾. The 789 gg and 218 qq̅ two-loop diagrams reduce to 417 masters. These are cast into ε-factorised differential equations spanning 13 elliptic curves and one genus-two curve, which lives in the non-planar sector nB463. Up to weight four, 300 of the 449 independent differential forms enter the finite remainder. None of the quadratic-type elliptic forms survive, but 55 of the 85 genus-two forms do. That is the basis for the “first genus-two finite remainder” claim; the curve itself had been identified earlier.

Boundary values are fixed at threshold. The authors run AMFlow at (x_1,x_2)=(10⁻⁴,2·10⁻⁴⁾ with 100–300 digits, match to generalised series, then fit constants with PSLQ. The elliptic and genus-two constants resist any known basis and are kept numerically. The public hqpAmp code evaluates renormalised finite remainders across phase space, switching between double and quad precision.

On practical impact, NNLO tt̅ already ran on numerical grids, and the qq̅ channel was already analytic. The gains here are: - control and speed; - 𝒪(ε¹,2) terms for three-loop IR studies; - a stress test of canonical-basis methods beyond elliptic.

The paper does not address bound-state effects. Its threshold expansions are fixed-order input that toponium-vs-continuum fits would still need to combine with a Coulomb/NRQCD treatment.

arXiv:2610.32845 — The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect (Isabel S. Sands et al.)

Sands and Hopkins analyse two FIRE-2 Milky Way analogs, m12f and m12m (m12i is dropped for its warped disk), with spectrally resolved CR transport. They compare each snapshot over 460–20 Myr lookback against a baseline “template”: the mean of the snapshots whose total ROI flux is below the median. For every ROI (10°, 20°) and line-of-sight cut (0, 2, 7 kpc), the Fermi GCE lies inside the 25th–75th percentile band of residuals, and many residuals are several times larger. One m12f snapshot matches the GCE in spectrum and is roughly spherical inside 10°, produced by at least three clustered supernova episodes. The physical driver is that CR diffusion across the central kpc takes ~1 Myr, comparable to the timescale of ISM disruption, so steady-state templates are structurally inadequate.

The caveats are substantial, and the authors state most of them: - Star formation. Central SFRs are 1–2 orders of magnitude above the CMZ, and total diffuse flux is a few to 10 times Fermi’s. The residual amplitude is therefore compared against a much brighter galaxy. - Sample size. There are only two galaxies and no AGN, so no frequency or look-elsewhere statistic can be computed. - Baseline choice. A baseline built from below-median snapshots biases residuals positive. - Comparison method. Residuals here are not a template fit; the authors’ proposed test is to run actual Fermi pipelines on the simulations.

A potentially useful discriminant is that the excesses are typically flanked by in-plane flux deficits.

arXiv:2610.31745 — FeynFacet: AI agents for analytic NLO QCD (Zhong-Bo Kang et al.)

Kang, Vogelsang and Zhang use LLM agents to write and run the process-specific programs for analytic NLO calculations. Physicists fix the observables, projections and HVBM conventions, and the finished programs run without further model calls. The pipeline: - spin and colour algebra done in parallel with FeynCalc, FORM and Tracer; - reverse unitarity for the real-emission phase space; - dimensional shifts to remove evanescent numerators; - Kira IBP at symbolic d, then SubTropica for the masters.

The new results are NLO transverse-spin-transfer hard functions: - all seven q^↑b→c^↑X classes through α_s³, including the regular-only q^↑g→q̅^↑X from identical-quark interference; - ℓq^↑→q^↑X through α_em²α_s, with the scattered lepton integrated.

They find σ̂_T,XX=σ̂_T,NN in every channel, so the spin dependence is purely cos(ϕ_a-ϕ_c).

Validation reproduces published UU/LL pp and ℓp results, double-transverse pp, and the one-loop TMD matching and soft functions. The checks on the new results are weaker than on the benchmarks: - The pp transfer results agree across the three algebra routes only at test points. Crossing from incoming-TT is symbolic only at Born level. - The ℓp result has no external benchmark, only Born normalisation, pole cancellation and RG checks. - All three routes share the same generated amplitudes, reduction and masters, so common-mode errors would go undetected.

As a test case for agentic theory work, the release of code alongside the coefficients is what makes it auditable.

item.title: Friday, October 23, 2026
item.description:
Same data, different error bars

Elmer et al. arXiv:2610.30239 reconstruct the triplet PDF three ways and get comparable central values with markedly different uncertainties. Morales-Zapien et al. arXiv:2610.30510 keep OGLE’s Magellanic events and efficiencies fixed and weaken the leading PBH bound by up to ~6× just by updating halo and lens models. Both carry the week’s error-budget thread, from scale variations to LZ’s ER tail, into ML fits and astrophysical limits. The sharpest measurement is Belle/Belle II’s first observation of Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺η, at a rate well above SU(3)_F expectations. There are no 248 keV papers today, the second blank day this week.

Themes

Assumptions inside the error bar

Elmer et al. arXiv:2610.30239 compare Gaussian processes, NN ensembles and tangent-kernel fits for the triplet PDF. Their normalised-bias diagnostic shows calibration depends on the correlations of the predictive covariance, not just its pointwise width. Morales-Zapien et al. arXiv:2610.30510 find the LMC halo is one of the levers on the microlensing bound, the same input this week’s LZ halo-tail fight turned on, and ask that compact-object limits be quoted with their modeling assumptions. Lind arXiv:2610.31103 simulates fictitious top mesons in Pythia 8.3 and puts the MC mass 240–330 MeV below the pole mass. That matters now that Ball et al. showed any threshold-excess number is also a statement about m_t.

Inference engines, sequential and pretrained

Bahl et al. arXiv:2610.30245 extend SBI from couplings to masses and widths by iteratively concentrating simulations where the data point. At equal training budget they get better-calibrated likelihoods for A→ZH and Y→HH. Magel et al.’s CURTAIN arXiv:2610.30894 and Li et al. arXiv:2610.31180 push foundation models into neutrino telescopes and TPC tracking. Hackett et al. arXiv:2610.30338 find that learned neutrino–nucleus cross sections need flux nuisances once appearance channels enter. This continues the month’s pattern of ML tooling moving from agents into the inference layer itself.

Axions, off the haloscope

Bottaro et al. arXiv:2610.30238 show ²²⁹Th nuclear clocks respond linearly to “imperfect” axions, where explicit PQ breaking or CEDMs shift the potential minimum. An Earth-sourced static field would also allow fifth-force searches. Bao et al. arXiv:2610.30250 treat the haloscope quantum mechanically. They find the photon-number distribution is not Poisson, and that a virialized Gaussian state can be told apart from a coherent state or BEC. Bose et al. arXiv:2610.30255 use supernova ALPs gravitationally bound to the remnant neutron star, whose decays reheat it. The cold PSR J2144−3933 then gives the strongest g_aγ limits at 1–400 MeV. Together they extend September’s widening of the axion program into new detection channels.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.31377: >10σ first observation, with a branching fraction “significantly larger” than SU(3) predictions. This is the third system this season where flavor-symmetry expectations strain, after B→PP and the ~60%-breaking B→DP fit, now in charm baryons.
  • arXiv:2610.30239: A clean closure-test anatomy of why ML PDF uncertainties disagree. Covariance in the likelihood, the kernel prior and NTK training stage are the knobs.
  • arXiv:2610.30510: Same events, weaker bound, and over 10× in a stress test. Anyone citing OGLE PBH limits should read which assumptions they inherited.
  • arXiv:2610.30894: The first neutrino-telescope pretraining task that scales and transfers to an unseen geometry. It cuts DeepIce’s angular error by 45%.
  • arXiv:2610.30238: Turns the quality of the PQ solution into a clock observable. It is a concrete strong-CP test outside EDMs.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.31254 A consistent neutrino determination of the low-energy weak mixing angle — M. Atzori Corona et al. (hep-ph). CEνNS plus ν–e give sin²θ_W=0.233⁺⁰.007_-0.006, independent of APV.
  • arXiv:2610.30754 Natural Chlorine Enhances Antineutrino Detection in the Deep Ocean — Ruike Cao et al. (hep-ex). Seawater chlorine’s ~8.6 MeV capture cascade pushes TRIDENT’s supernova reach past 100 kpc.
  • arXiv:2610.31316 Charmed baryon-to-meson ratios inside jets… — Zi-Xuan Xu et al. (hep-ph). The sign of the in-jet Λ_c/D⁰ modification separates color reconnection from coalescence, a handle on small-system baryon enhancement.
  • arXiv:2610.31534 Testing charged Simpson-Visser-AdS spacetimes with twin-peak QPOs — Saeed Ullah Khan et al. (gr-qc). The authors concede the fitted “charge” probably just absorbs the neglected spin.
  • arXiv:2610.31458 Evidence for Kaluza-Klein excitations of the graviton, gluon and quark at LHC — Alain Le Yaouanc et al. (hep-ph). The CMS four-jet excesses read as KK gluons. The lighter one needs existing limits to be wrong.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.31377 — Measurements of the branching fractions of Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺π⁰ and Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺η decays at Belle and Belle II (Belle et al.)

Belle and Belle II (980 + 570 fb⁻¹) report the first observation of Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺η at >10σ statistical significance, from 1107 ± 45 signal events. Relative to the reference mode, the measured ratio is ℬ/ℬ(Λπ⁺π⁰⁾⁼⁽⁸.73±0.35±0.43)×10⁻³, giving ℬ=(6.20±0.25±0.31±0.30)×10⁻⁴. The three SU(3)_F predictions are (1.9±0.6), (0.45±0.10) and (0.59±0.24)×10⁻⁴. The measurement exceeds them by 5.5σ, 11.2σ and 10.1σ respectively. The companion SCS mode is measured as ℬ(ΛK⁺π⁰⁾⁼⁽¹.29±0.05±0.05±0.06)×10⁻³. This agrees with BESIII and with the 2024 fit that includes the color-symmetric Hamiltonian (1.36 ± 0.25), and sits well below the earlier 3.5–4.5 × 10⁻³ predictions. The precision is markedly improved over BESIII’s ±0.27 statistical error.

So the same SU(3)_F fit that now gets ΛK⁺π⁰ right undershoots ΛK⁺η by an order of magnitude. That is the charm-baryon entry in the season’s flavor-symmetry strain noted in the digest. The caveat is visible in the paper itself. The two-body invariant-mass spectra deviate significantly from phase space, and efficiencies are reweighted to the data Dalitz distribution. The predictions assume non-resonant, S-wave-dominated meson pairs, so intermediate resonances in ΛK⁺η (smaller phase space) could account for the excess rather than a failure of the symmetry itself. A Dalitz analysis would discriminate. On the experimental side, the η systematic is dominated by photon reconstruction (4.4%), and there is a 4.8% reference-BF uncertainty.

arXiv:2610.30239 — Faithful Uncertainties in ML-Based Inverse Problems: GPs, NNs and NTKs for the Triplet PDF (Nina Elmer et al.)

Methods that agree on the central T_3 disagree on what their error bars mean. The setup is a closure test on BCDMS F_2^p-F_2^d, using 248 points with the full covariance, NNPDF4.0 truth, and a data region of x≳0.07. The normalised bias R_b is computed on a single L_1 realisation:

Model R_b (full covariance) R_b (diagonal only)
RBF GP 1.08 0.38
Gibbs GP 0.86 0.53
NTK, trained 0.67 —
NTK, at initialisation 9.5 —
L_2 NN ensemble 0.74 —
L_1 NN ensemble 2.84 —

The L_1 ensemble excludes data uncertainty by construction, so its large value is expected. Dropping covariance correlations shifts R_b non-monotonically, so pointwise width alone does not determine calibration. Two other failure modes stand out: - Heteroscedastic loss. It learns broad diagonal variances, which the authors read as likelihood misspecification rather than faithful uncertainty. - Endpoint preprocessing. It sets the small-x answer. The fit at α=1 versus α=0.5 is identical in the data region but diverges below 0.07. Preprocessed GP variance vanishes at the endpoints by construction, giving bands that miss the truth.

In the HERA extrapolation test, the initialisation NTK degrades NC-EM by Δn_σ≈5.0, while all other models stay below 1. The authors are candid about the limits. With n_eig = 4–19, the test rules out gross underestimates but cannot certify faithfulness. A single seed visibly changes the reconstructions, and the L_2 ensemble is only NNPDF-inspired.

arXiv:2610.30510 — Same Events, Weaker Bound: Model Dependence in Magellanic Microlensing Limits on Primordial Black Holes (David Morales-Zapien et al.)

The authors hold OGLE’s 13 events, efficiencies and t_E posteriors fixed and change only the rate model, inside OGLE’s own relaxed likelihood. The benchmark uses a flattened MW halo (q_h=0.72, ρ_⊙=0.30 GeV cm⁻³), a cored Burkert LMC halo, Ibata disks, and a lighter LMC with a shallower IMF. It weakens the 20-year relaxed limit by up to 1.6 near 0.32 M_⊙. A deliberately extreme stress test weakens it by up to 3.4.

The headline “~6×” (6.2 for the benchmark, 13.2 for the stress test) is relative to the strict limit, so it also folds in OGLE’s own event-origin difference. In the planetary-mass window, the factors are 1.19 and 2.39 for smooth PBHs, and 3.4 and 6.0 for 30 pc clusters under a Lyα shot-noise cap. A one-at-a-time ablation at 0.45 M_⊙ shows the IMF matters most (R=0.68), while the heavier disks push the other way (1.10). LMC-induced disequilibrium raises the lensing-weighted halo density by about 6%, undercutting a common critique.

The caveats are explicit: - Parameters were chosen to suppress the rate and are fixed, not marginalized. - The IMF endpoints are not a joint confidence region. - The stress test conflicts with 6D tracer masses. - Its isothermal LMC halo fails the LMC mass constraints.

Oddly, the weaker limits coexist with a larger preference for nonzero f near 0.03 M_⊙: Δχ²⁼⁹.2–10.2, versus 3.7 in OGLE’s analysis.

item.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026
item.description:
Neutrino mixing doesn’t run observably

Barenboim et al. arXiv:2610.28744 argue that a growing literature on observable RG running of neutrino mixing makes one mistake. That literature proposes zero-distance flavor change, shifted CP phases and odd astrophysical flavor ratios. In the authors’ account, mixing is fixed by the on-shell self-energy, and setting μ=Q only reintroduces large logs that undo the running. They check this in the MSSM, two seesaw models and SMEFT, and add a data bound: short-baseline experiments already limit any angle change between production and detection to 0.7°–2.4°. The day’s other result with direct consequences is a Gaia-anchored halo tail that undercuts last week’s halo rescue of the LZ Higgsino.

Themes

LZ: the halo tail gets measured

X. Zhang et al. arXiv:2610.28731 combine a Gaia-reconstructed Milky Way with FIRE-2’s best LMC analog. They find no local dark matter faster than ~900 km/s, and the inferred LZ splitting moves by up to ~130 keV depending on the tail. That matters because Graham et al. (10-16) could rescue the thermal Higgsino from the solar-capture bound only with a tail extended to 1100 km/s. If this reconstruction holds, that tail is not there.

Two papers sit around it: - Ibe et al. arXiv:2610.29335 avoid the Sun by going heavy, to a 10²–10⁴ TeV pseudo-Dirac doublet. Making it compatible with non-thermal leptogenesis takes fine-tuned CP violation. - Chiang et al.’s PIANISTpy arXiv:2610.28758 supplies differentiable anisotropic velocity distributions beyond Maxwell–Boltzmann.

Neutrino corrections and fits

  • Double-β radiative corrections. de Vries et al. arXiv:2610.28742 find these bias ξ_31 extractions and raise the 0νββ rate by ~5%. Real-photon emission is central, and they ask experiments to simulate it, which extends the week’s error-budget thread to nuclear decays.
  • Low primordial helium. Guo et al. arXiv:2610.29069 read EMPRESS’s low Y_P as non-unitary mixing (α_22=0.982), though standard N_eff remains allowed.
  • Statistics and unfolding. Coloma et al. arXiv:2610.28681 extend the parameter goodness-of-fit test to data sets that share a prior. Chen et al. arXiv:2608.16107 unfold the sub-IBP reactor flux from CEνNS data using halo-independent techniques.

Taggers, smaller still

Agarwal et al. arXiv:2610.29439 distill six teachers, including two foundation models, into small students. A 2k-parameter L-GATr-slim matches ParT. This follows yesterday’s SParTA, which matched ParT with one-seventh the parameters, so the compression keeps going. Abasov et al. arXiv:2610.29678 apply LGaTr to top-event reconstruction.

CP that EDMs miss

Keus arXiv:2610.28790 builds C-violating, P-conserving CP sources that cannot feed EDMs, relevant to baryogenesis. That echoes yesterday’s argument that a cancelled electron EDM still leaves collider-visible τ dipoles. Yu et al. arXiv:2610.29819 project A_CP^Λ at 10⁻⁴ and a Λ EDM at 10⁻²⁰ e·cm from entangled ΛΛ̅ at STCF.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.28744: A direct refutation of a whole class of proposed signatures. Expect replies.
  • arXiv:2610.28731: The halo input every 248 keV paper now needs, covering all NREFT operators.
  • arXiv:2610.28742: The double-weak Sirlin function differs substantially from two single-β ones. Experimental 2νββ spectral analyses should check it.
  • arXiv:2610.29439: Released weights. It also shows that same-size students can differ almost 10× in inference speed.
  • arXiv:2610.29726: Chu et al. extract 14 nonzero-skewness GFFs from the lattice with a neural-network t-parametrization, giving J^u-d=0.296(11)(7). It extends September’s lattice-GPD run.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.28704 Gauge Field Fluctuations Protect the Higgs Vacuum When a Small Universe Begins — Alan Zhang (hep-ph). A sequel to his Casimir-turning-point cosmology from 10-20, now with Higgs-vacuum survival for m_t<172.96 GeV.
  • arXiv:2610.29354 B_sJ(6114) as a Higher-Partial-Wave K̅^B⁽) Molecular Candidate — Shiquan Zhang et al. (hep-ph). The decay widths favor 1⁻.
  • arXiv:2610.28730 Can componentwise D7-tadpole cancellation yield a chiral Standard Model?… — Mudit Jain (hep-th). No, for smooth O7⁻ orientifolds.
  • arXiv:2610.29973 NTL amplification in a SuperCDMS-style detector fabricated from a University of South Dakota-grown germanium crystal — Dongming Mei et al. (physics.ins-det). An 8.9× gain, but only after a 600 nm Al contact was deposited.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.28744 — The renormalization-group running of neutrino mixing is undetectable (Gabriela Barenboim et al.)

Barenboim, Bustamante and Liu argue that every experiment measures one physical mixing matrix Û. They define it by the eigenvectors of the on-shell physical mass matrix m_eff=m(μ)+Σ_M-12(Σ_K^Tm+mΣ_K), which does not depend on μ. Momentum transfer Q never flows through the external-leg self-energy. If one sets μ=Q, that self-energy picks up ln(Q²/M_X²⁾ terms that rotate U(Q) back to Û. The premise in the prior literature keeps U(Q) but drops these logs, which the authors call an inconsistent truncation.

Only vertex and box corrections carry both flavor and Q dependence, and they lack the 1/(m_i-m_j) degeneracy enhancement. The paper gives their sizes in each setting: - MSSM: a flavor-diagonal ~0.7% rescaling of the ν_τ coupling at 10 TeV. - GeV HNL: at most 4×10⁻⁹. - Light-scalar seesaw: zero at one loop.

For Model 2 of Babu et al., the claimed running disappears once the Dirac masses are allowed to run along with Y_N.

Independently of the theory argument, NuTeV and NOMAD limits on zero-baseline transitions would require |Δθ_23|<0.7^∘, |Δθ_12|<2.3^∘, |Δθ_13|<2.4^∘ and |Δδ_CP|<16^∘ between m_π and a few GeV, if the premise held. This bound excludes the β_δ=0.15 used to illustrate a proposed reactor signal.

Caveats: - The data bounds assume one parameter shifts at a time, so correlated shifts could partly compensate. - They do not apply when running starts above a few GeV, as in the MSSM case or the ~5 GeV double-bang configuration. There only the theory argument applies. - Off-diagonal vertex terms beyond the SM, up to ~10⁻², survive and act as non-standard charged-current interactions. - Two of the targeted papers are the authors’ own, including a step-at-Q=M HNL paper they now say also used an incorrect δm. That self-correction gives the refutation more weight.

arXiv:2610.28731 — Simulation-Informed High-Velocity Dark Matter in the Effective Theory of Direct Detection (Xiuyuan Zhang et al.)

Zhang, Herrera, Thoyas and Necib build a local dark matter (DM) velocity distribution from two pieces: - a Gaia DR3 reconstruction, combining Gaia–Sausage–Enceladus stars convolved with a simulation-calibrated kernel and a generalized-Gaussian diffuse component; - the m12b LMC analog from FIRE-2, which contributes 32 particles at 738–846 km/s and 0.3% of the local density.

The resulting laboratory-frame endpoints, and the maximum accessible splitting δ_max for a 1 TeV particle on xenon, are:

Distribution Endpoint (km/s) δ_max (keV)
Standard Halo Model (SHM) 793 381
Reconstruction alone 835 423
Reconstruction + LMC 846 434
Auriga-25 (Au-25) 975 575

Limits across all 14 non-relativistic EFT operators coincide below δ≈200 keV and then fan out. Velocity-suppressed operators separate first.

For 𝒪_1, the region that fits the LZ 248 keV event plus empty sidebands sits at different splittings: - SHM: δ=304–360 keV. - FIRE-based: 320–390 keV. - Au-25: 376–448 keV, with mass confined to 171–468 GeV.

In the digest’s context, a tail reaching 1100 km/s would need support well beyond anything here.

The authors are explicit that the result is limited: - The tail rests on 32 particles. - The Sun has to be placed out of the disk to match the LMC geometry. With the observer in the disk, the LMC particles come out slower. - The Milky Way-only endpoint has a 16–84% posterior spread of 773–912 km/s. - Their counting likelihood differs from LZ’s published limits by up to ~3×. - They conclude that a single LMC analog cannot define the tail uniquely.

arXiv:2610.28742 — Radiative corrections to double-β decay and their impact on experimental analyses (Jordy de Vries et al.)

This is the full companion to the authors’ earlier Letter. In a heavy-nucleus EFT with explicit 1⁺ intermediate states, de Vries, Mereghetti, el Morabit and Sandner compute all 𝒪(α) virtual and real corrections for arbitrary excitation energy ω_n. They also give new closed-form heavy-propagator triangle and box integrals via an auxiliary-mass trick.

Main structural results: - No Z-enhanced terms survive. The 𝒪(αZ) and 𝒪(αZ²⁾ terms cancel class by class, except the static Coulomb piece already contained in the Fermi functions. - A new topology matters. The electron–electron box has no single-β analogue and brings in dependence on the two-electron invariant mass s. - The correction factorizes at large ω_n. At leading order in 1/ω_n it is the tree-level rate times a “double-weak Sirlin function” f_2ν(β_1,β_2,β_12). This function differs from the sum of two single-β Sirlin functions, and its μ dependence cancels against g_V⁴ (g_V-1≈1.9–2.0% at μ=2E_0). - One new nuclear input appears at next order. It is ζ_31, a log-weighted M_GT ratio, which the authors find negligible. - There is a non-trivial check. The total-visible-energy spectrum has no lnm_e dependence as m_e→0, as the Kinoshita–Lee–Nauenberg theorem requires.

Because the electron-only and calorimetric (ϵ_tot) spectra differ, the correction depends on how a detector handles the real photon. The authors provide the fully differential photon spectrum and ask experiments to simulate it. For 0νββ, the inclusive rate rises by ~5%, independent of the nuclear matrix elements and m_ββ.

The extracted text ends before the numerical ξ_31-bias results, so their size cannot be quoted here.

Acknowledged approximations: - 𝒪(αZRE_e) finite-size terms are not yet mapped rigorously. - The Fermi function F is also used for the β_1β_2y_12 term. - The 1/ω_n expansion holds for ¹³⁶Xe, but the authors cite larger deviations for ⁸²Se.

item.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026
item.description:
LZ’s background gets audited

For seven weeks the 248 keV literature has treated LZ’s background estimate as fixed and argued only about which dark-matter model survives solar capture. Bandyopadhyay et al. arXiv:2610.27105 question that estimate. Rebuilding the electron-recoil continuum from LZ’s released simulation configuration, they find the published calibration does not constrain the response tail at the probabilities that matter. Tails that match the executable model to 0.47% in the N_e quantiles make the ER contribution comparable to the whole quoted background in the comparison region. This is not a claim that the tail is wrong, and they list the measurements that would settle it. Still, it is the first paper to put the event’s significance itself on the table. Elsewhere, birefringence attracts two new sources and τ physics gets a set of future-collider projections.

Themes

Birefringence finds new fields

Minotti et al. arXiv:2610.27082 source the signal from a subdominant stiff (w=1) pseudoscalar. BBN and cluster-quasar conversion squeeze g_ϕγ into 8.9×10⁻¹⁴–5.0×10⁻¹³ GeV⁻¹, a window astrophysical axion searches can close. Bagherian et al. arXiv:2610.27059 get birefringence from axion–monopole dynamics, in the same parameter space that fits DESI’s phantom-like dark energy. Both join Kasai’s lepton-asymmetry route (10-09) as alternatives to an axion explanation of the year’s 3.5σ post-dust signal.

τ at future colliders

Allwicher et al. arXiv:2610.27057 find that FCC-ee’s 2×10¹¹ τ pairs improve τ→3ℓ and ℓγ limits by 30–800×. That beats Z→τℓ on reach and on operator coverage, though h→τℓ wins for Yukawa-like operators. Senol et al. arXiv:2610.28147 project |a_τ|≲3.4×10⁻⁴ at FCC-hh, more than ten times looser than Buttazzo’s FCC-ee threshold projection from 10-12. Liu et al. arXiv:2610.28400 connect electron EDMs to timelike τ dipoles.

Taggers under budgets

Cox et al.’s LEAF arXiv:2610.27078 runs a LUT-aware linformer at 35 ns and 28k LUTs for trigger-level jet tagging. Baruah et al.’s SParTA arXiv:2610.27106 matches ParT on quark–gluon tagging with one-seventh the parameters, by giving full attention only to the hard core of the jet.

DGLAP as a curve, twice

Kou et al. arXiv:2610.27886 and Bondarenko et al. arXiv:2610.28115 independently put LO DGLAP on the Fisher–Rao manifold on the same day. The first finds a near-small-circle trajectory; the second derives a closed-form lower bound on the evolution speed. Neither changes a fit, but the coincidence is notable.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.27105: If the ER tail is this loosely constrained, every model built on the 248 keV kinematics inherits that uncertainty. The proposed calibrations are what to watch.
  • arXiv:2610.28506: Bashir et al. compute the missing isospin-breaking ρππ correction, Δa_μ=-2.32(1.64)×10⁻¹⁰, for the τ route into the lattice-vs-data-driven HVP fight.
  • arXiv:2610.28283: Price automates amplitude-level YFS exponentiation in Sherpa for general processes. At 𝒪(α²⁾, two matchings agree to ~10⁻³, which makes it FCC-ee infrastructure.
  • arXiv:2610.27346: Bhattacharya shows jet acceptance sets a hard bound on hadronic W polarization tagging. Production kinematics carry more information than decay angles, so event-level taggers win.
  • arXiv:2610.28400: A four-loop result showing that a cancelled electron EDM still leaves an absorptive timelike τ signal. Colliders can probe the blind direction.

From the community

  • arXiv:2610.28505 Blueprint for an AI-Enabled Particle Theory Community — George T. Fleming et al. (hep-ph). Recommendations for a community-scale AI effort tied to the Genesis Mission, following last week’s formalization position paper.
  • arXiv:2610.28296 Open Science with the LHCb Ntupling Service — Christine A. Aidala et al. (hep-ex). On-demand custom ntuples from over 4 PB, including Run 2 data for the first time.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.27270 Correlations in oscillation data and their impact on neutrino mixing models — Janusz Gluza et al. (hep-ph). Most mixing schemes fit IO better and TM₂ is out at >3σ. That is awkward next to today’s replacement of Jin et al.’s 3.3σ normal-ordering result.
  • arXiv:2610.28014 Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition… — Deeksha Dattaram Naik et al. (hep-ph). LZ 2024 excludes the entire transition-viable singlet sector.
  • arXiv:2610.27236 Searching for Dense Perturbers in Cold Dark Matter Simulations — Xingyu Zhang et al. (astro-ph.CO). None of 5000+ CDM subhalos is dense enough to match the observed perturbers.
  • arXiv:2610.27056 Annihilation feedback on elastic scattering in self-interacting dark matter — Kalliopi Petraki et al. (hep-ph). With its companion arXiv:2610.27089, it uses unitarity to tie elastic SIDM cross sections to annihilation and bound-state formation.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.27105: The Electron-Recoil Response Tail and the LZ High-Energy Event Background

The published LZ response does not fix the ER leakage that the 248 keV event’s background estimate depends on. The authors rebuild the ER continuum from NEST’s EFT2024 configuration and get a per-decay leakage of P≃1.3×10⁻⁷ at a 4.1σ displacement in N_e. That yields N^ER_leak=(1.9±0.1±0.4)×10⁻⁴ counts, against LZ’s 0.0106 total in the 500<S1c<600 phd region. They then construct three families of distributions (generalised-normal, skew-t, Johnson S_U) that match the executable model’s mean, variance and skewness exactly. The families agree within a factor of ~2 at matched quantile deviation, yet the tail probability spans more than five orders of magnitude.

The thresholds are close to the model:

  • 0.14% quantile agreement: ER reaches 10% of the quoted background.
  • 0.47%: ER equals the whole quoted background.
  • 1.10%: ER reaches 0.1 counts.

LZ’s counter-argument, that no events appear between the event and the ER band, does not discriminate between these tails. Even the heaviest family predicts only 0.69 events in that gap. Two further points:

  • Printed vs. implemented response. The printed Supplement Eq. 4 gives a fluctuation width 1.475× the implemented one. Taken literally, it implies 0.60 ER counts, far above LZ’s quoted total for all backgrounds.
  • Calibration reach. The tritium and ¹⁴C calibrations stop at S1c = 500 phd, while the event sits at 540 phd.

Caveats. The authors explicitly do not claim the tail is wrong, and they do not propagate the result to LZ’s 2.6σ global (3.4σ local) significance. The link between the NEST commit and the Letter is circumstantial. The ER selection efficiency is unpublished. The ¹²⁴Xe/¹²⁵I lines are excluded.

What would settle it. A tail measurement at the 10⁻⁵ level near N_q∼5×10³, or a shape fit using ~3×10³ events per slice (rising to 3×10⁴ for the mildest problematic tail).

arXiv:2610.28506: Isospin breaking in ρππ couplings

The missing isospin-breaking (IB) ρππ coupling correction comes out small and cuts the corresponding τ-route uncertainty to roughly a third of the White Paper’s assumed ±4.7×10⁻¹⁰. The method is a symmetry-preserving Dyson–Schwinger/Bethe–Salpeter contact-interaction model. IB enters dynamically through flavour-dependent beyond-rainbow-ladder couplings ξ_u,d, tuned to Δm_ρ, and explicitly through m_d/m_u∈[1,2]. Results:

  • Coupling ratio: g_ρ⁰ππ/g_ρ⁺ππ=1.0024(17)(1).
  • Width difference: ΔΓ_ρ=+0.39(51) MeV, compatible with but tighter than PDG (+0.31 ± 1.3) and a data-based extraction (−0.58 ± 1.01).
  • Effect on a_μ: the ρππ term is Δa_μ=-2.32(1.64)×10⁻¹⁰, about one-third of the White Paper’s error.

The −2.32 is not the net shift. It nearly cancels against the radiative-correction term (−2.22) and the pion-mass phase-space term (+4.09). The total form-factor-ratio IB is -0.25(1.64)×10⁻¹⁰, compared with the older -1.62(65)×10⁻¹⁰.

Caveats. - The contact interaction is a crude kernel; the symmetric coupling comes out at 6.29 against 5.94 from the PDG width. - The error is driven almost entirely by the poorly known input Δm_ρ=0.7(0.8) MeV. - The τ-side numbers rely on a Gounaris–Sakurai parametrisation. - The same framework predicts R_ϕ=1.484±0.029, 2.2σ below BESIII.

arXiv:2610.28283: Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC

The extracted text cuts off before the validation section, so the headline numbers here come from the abstract.

ACRAIC brings coherent (CEEX-style) amplitude-level YFS exponentiation to general processes inside Sherpa. Previously this existed only for hand-coded fermion-pair production in KKMC. The generalisation works in three steps:

  • Photon assignment. The initial/final assignment of photons becomes an assignment to emission stages. Gauge invariance forces these stages to be partitions of the charged legs into charge-neutral sets, including resonance stages for Z/γ^* and W pairs.
  • Remainders. The infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with N+2 and N+3 legs and partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by Comix’s Berends–Giele recursion.
  • Virtual correction. The one-loop electroweak virtual enters as a per-helicity factor from OpenLoops or Recola.

Validation is against KKMC for e⁺e⁻→μ⁺μ⁻ at photonic 𝒪(α²⁾. Comparison is also made with the squared-level YFS_NLO_EW, which shares the resummation and differs only in matching. At 𝒪(α²⁾ the two matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to ~10⁻³, and the perturbative uncertainty drops about tenfold relative to 𝒪(α). The author reports that squared-level matching can go unstable in four-lepton production while the amplitude-level version stays stable. Example applications are the FCC-ee Higgs recoil mass and Z-pole distributions.

Caveats. - “Photonic 𝒪(α²⁾” omits two-loop γZ boxes and weak corrections. - The paper is described as mostly technical, with phenomenology left to dedicated studies.

item.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026
item.description:
Gell-Mann’s weak magnetism, seen in the neutron

Camarasa-Domene et al. arXiv:2610.26792 separate the weak-magnetism form factor from λ by combining β-asymmetry data with the neutron lifetime and superallowed ℱt values. They get g_M=4.47(87) against the CVC prediction of 4.71, and exclude zero at 5.1σ. The significance stays between 5.0 and 6.1σ across variations of the neutron dataset, despite its known internal tensions. This is a reanalysis of existing data rather than a new measurement, but it is a clean one. Elsewhere, IceCube delivers precision rather than limits, the Galactic Center excess meets the dwarfs, and LZ model-building returns after yesterday’s zero.

Themes

IceCube, measuring

Hajjar et al. arXiv:2610.24068 measure the ν_μ CC cross section from 150 GeV to 40 TeV at under 20% uncertainty, consistent with the SM. Above 1 TeV they see a first mild hint that ν and ν̄ can be separated. Lamoureux et al. arXiv:2610.25214 find a 1.9σ preference for linear Lorentz-invariance violation at Λ_LIV=5.8×10¹⁷ GeV in HESE–GRB timing, driven by the subluminal component. That is far from last week’s Planck-scale decoherence exclusion in strength. Noriega et al. arXiv:2610.26654 find that DESI plus CMB-SPA disfavors strongly self-interacting neutrinos at odds of 5:100000.

The Galactic Center, and LZ again

Kim et al. arXiv:2610.26648 test 18 years of Fermi data against 80 diffuse models. In their best-fit model, limits from 30 dwarf spheroidals exclude the 68% GCE regions for bb̅, cc̅, light quarks, gluons, 4b and 2b2τ. Only τ-rich channels and light-mediator 4b cascades survive. Last week Abazajian et al. argued against a shared origin for the halo excess and the LZ event. Kim et al. arXiv:2610.25423 build exactly that shared origin anyway: in their exothermic dark-Higgs model, the 26 GeV dark-photon branch matches the southern-sky GCE, and CMB limits exclude the 1 GeV branch at its likelihood minimum. Tan et al. arXiv:2610.25925 find a 1.85 GeV [ud][ds][su] hexaquark for the invisible-dibaryon reading of LZ, which they concede depends on the OPE truncation.

Flavor symmetry, broken on purpose

With SU(3)_F breaking now the week’s pressure point (60% in B→DP), Wen et al. arXiv:2610.24975 derive charmed-baryon U-spin sum rules valid at first order in the breaking. He et al. arXiv:2610.26175 propose using production processes that select a flavor representation to separate the two poles of the D_0^*(2300). BESIII arXiv:2610.26673 gives the first strong–EM relative phase in J/ψ→Σ⁺Σ̅⁻, at about ±108°±25°.

Error budgets, formalized

The Aspen writeup by Canonero et al. arXiv:2610.25091 argues for supplementing 7-point scale variations with known missing higher-order terms. That is the policy version of last week’s lesson from cold-QED N³LO, where scale bands understated the true error. Li et al. arXiv:2610.26130 use the correlation between hadronic contributions to a_e and a_μ to attack the lattice vs. data-driven HVP gap, which ETMC widened last week. Kotikov et al. arXiv:2610.25135 extract α_s=0.1177⁺²⁷_-25 from hadron multiplicities.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.26792: A seventy-year-old CVC prediction finally observed in the free neutron. The robustness to the lifetime tensions is the part to check.
  • arXiv:2610.24068: One measurement covering accelerator to astrophysical energies at under 20%. It will become the reference curve for TeV cross sections.
  • arXiv:2610.26648: The most systematic dSph-vs-GCE comparison in a while. It leaves a narrow, τ-flavored corridor for dark-matter readings.
  • arXiv:2610.25091: Concrete prescriptions beyond scale variation, plus a frequentist treatment of non-Gaussian theory errors. Likely to be cited in experimental systematics sections.
  • arXiv:2610.25216: Escribano et al.’s four-state mixing fit favors a radially excited non-strange state over gluonium in the η′. It is a second glueball reading weakened this month, after the X(2370) reassessment.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.26188 Measurements of time-dependent b-hadron properties in LHCb — Lucas Foreman (hep-ex). These proceedings include the first time-dependent CPV measurement in b→sℓℓ (B_s→K_Sμμ, S=+0.82±0.29) and an LHCb ϕ_s average of -41±17 mrad.
  • arXiv:2610.24954 ceci n’est pas un tagger, can an LLM flavour-tag a jet? — Andrea Coccaro et al. (hep-ex). With code-writing forbidden, an LLM still achieves non-trivial b/c/light/τ discrimination, and its stated rationales track the truth flavor.
  • arXiv:2610.24634 Common origin of the Belle-BESIII line-shape difference… — Cheng-Xi Liu et al. (hep-ph). Radiative higher-charmonium production leaking into Belle’s ISR samples could explain three discrepant line shapes.
  • arXiv:2610.24905 A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe — Alan Zhang (gr-qc). A cosmic beginning that a top pole mass above 173.7 GeV would exclude, making it testable at FCC-ee.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.26792 — First observation of weak magnetism in neutron decay (Miriam Camarasa-Domene et al.)

The weak-magnetism form factor comes out as g_M = 4.47(87), which excludes g_M=0 at 5.1σ and sits 0.3σ from the CVC value of 4.71. The β asymmetry alone cannot separate g_M from λ. The authors fix λ= -1.27598(61) independently, using r_nτ_n(1+3λ²⁾⁼²ℱt with: - τ_n=878.36(43) s, the PDG bottle average with S=1.81; - ℱt=3070.01(1.90) s from ²⁶mAl alone, reanalyzed with updated charge radii.

They then reinterpret the asymmetry data as an effective Ã that carries explicit g_M dependence. Two refinements matter: - They evaluate the energy moments over each experiment’s actual window rather than the full phase space. This raises the g_M sensitivity relative to the earlier 3σ global fit. - The linearized version, g_M = 4.40(50)_ℱt(39)_τ_n(59)_Ã, shows that all three inputs contribute comparably to the error.

The robustness checks are the main content. The significance ranges across dataset choices as follows:

Dataset choice g_M Significance
Lifetime set including beam values (S=2.3) 4.63(92) 5.0σ
Adding the a, B, λ_AB correlations 4.85(85) 5.7σ
PERKEO III + UCNτ only 4.68(81) 5.8σ
Post-2012 asymmetries only (no scale factor needed) 5.00(82) 6.1σ

Fitting the spectral shape of A(E_e) would tighten σ(g_M) by only 3–7%, based on Asimov studies. A recast of the PERKEO III Fierz likelihood gives a consistent 5.07(92).

Caveats: - The baseline ℱt rests on a single transition. It carries a δ_NS error (1.44 s) that is comparable to its statistical error. - The λ determination relies on the SM relation between τ_n and ℱt. The result is therefore a consistency test within the SM, not a model-independent extraction.

arXiv:2610.24068 — Measurement of the neutrino cross section across the TeV scale using IceCube data (Rasmi Hajjar et al.)

The analysis uses only the public eight-year IceCube upgoing-track sample: 305,735 events, more than 99.9% pure ν_μ CC. It extracts the average ν/ν̄ CC cross section in five bins from 150 GeV to 40 TeV. Earth absorption and the event energy distribution break the flux–cross-section degeneracy. Relative to CSMS, the normalizations are:

Bin Normalization
0.15–0.36 TeV 1.11⁺⁰.12_-0.13
0.36–1.17 TeV 1.22⁺⁰.24_-0.17
1.17–3.79 TeV 1.11⁺⁰.15_-0.12
3.79–12.3 TeV 0.92⁺⁰.15_-0.12
12.3–40 TeV 1.01⁺⁰.15_-0.13

All bins are within 20% and consistent with the SM. This bridges the energy-resolved collider points (up to about 2 TeV) and the astrophysical ones (above about 10 TeV). Between 360 GeV and 2 TeV the uncertainties already beat FASER’s.

Freeing ν and ν̄ separately gives a non-zero ν̄ cross section above 360 GeV at only 1.6σ (p = 0.06). That drops to 1.1σ if σ_ν>σ_ν̅ is enforced, because it is partly driven by an anticorrelated swap in bin 4 (ν: 0.40, ν̄: 2.1).

The main caveat for anyone treating this as a reference curve is the first bin. It carries a 16% Gaussian prior from fixed-target data, and that prior anchors the atmospheric flux normalization. Without it: - the fit prefers a lower flux; - the other four bins shift up by 20–30%; - the first bin lands about 2σ above CSMS.

So the result is limited by the flux–cross-section anticorrelation and is partly calibrated by accelerator input. A tenfold exposure forecast gives under 10% on the average cross section and more than 7σ for ν̄.

arXiv:2610.26648 — Dark Matter Interpretations of the Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess with 18 Years of Fermi-LAT Data and the FL16Y Source Catalog (Sang Hwan Kim et al.)

The GCE is re-extracted from 17.7 years of FRONT-only data with FL16Y masks, scanning 80 GALPROP diffuse models. Model X fits best, ahead of the next model by Δ(-2lnℒ)=72. Systematics come from a full 14×14 covariance built from 22 Galactic-plane control regions.

Against new combined limits from 30 dwarfs, with J-factor uncertainties profiled, the picture is: - bb̅ and other hadronic channels: the best fit is (39.5 GeV, 1.2×10⁻²⁶ cm³/s) with χ² = 27.5/12. Its entire 68% region lies above the dSph limit, as do those for cc̅, light quarks and gluons. - Effective four-body channels: the 68% regions for 4b and 2b2τ are fully excluded. - τ⁺τ⁻: the best fit (9.3 GeV, χ² = 22.8/12) sits just 0.67% above the limit, and part of its 68% region survives. - 4τ: the best fit is 8.7% above the limit, and part of its 68% region survives. - 4b cascades: these fit best near r=m_ϕ/m_χ≃0.3. Per the abstract, part of the 68% region stays below the limits for r≲0.4.
