arXiv:2609.28700 — Measuring Dual-Superconductor Length Scales in the QCD Vacuum at HERA (Tobias Toll et al.)

Toll and Vasim replace Gaussian hotspots with Clem’s vortex profile, K_0(√(b²⁺ξ_v²⁾/λ), in a Good–Walker dipole model. Coherent and incoherent moments are computed analytically, with log-normal saturation-scale fluctuations. They fit all 104 H1/ZEUS J/ψ photoproduction points (67 coherent, 37 incoherent; |t|<30 GeV², 40≤W≤251 GeV) and get χ²/ndf=70.8/98 at N_hs=8.

The extracted vacuum parameters are: - λ=0.191(5)(19) fm and ξ_v=0.087(5)(12) fm. - κ=2.7(3)(7), which is type-II. - 1/λ=1.03(11) GeV, compared with the lattice 1⁺⁻ gluelump at 0.87(15) GeV. The authors note that the gluelump value is scheme-dependent.

The Ginzburg–Landau string tension reproduces √(σ_0) for α_S=0.37(9), close to α_S(1/λ²⁾⁼⁰.36(2). Alternative tails (stretched exponential, power law) worsen the fit by Δχ²⁼³⁰. A floating tail exponent returns n=1.17(15), consistent with the K_0 value of 1.

Caveats: - The scalar sector fits less well. m_S=√(2)/ξ=3.9(7) GeV is 2.4(4)× the 0⁺⁺ glueball. - The dominant uncertainty comes from the weak sensitivity to N_hs. - A free normalization, about 1.2, is floated. - The type-II prediction of vortex repulsion cannot be tested, because saturation fluctuations are degenerate with geometric variance at |t|∼1 GeV². M_Y tagging at the EIC would break this degeneracy.

The claimed Q² independence is a clean EIC/LHeC test.

arXiv:2609.29442 — Hidden Region Finder (Einan Gardi)

Neither the full text nor the abstract of this paper was supplied, so there is no deep dive. See the digest line for why it

Citation radar

The radar this week is a single story. All four papers are responses to LZ230616, the lone ~248 keV nuclear recoil LZ reported at 2.6σ global (3.4σ local) significance, and all four were posted within about 48 hours of one another. Their bibliographies overlap almost completely, and much of each count probably reflects the reflexive “see also Refs. [x–y]” citing typical of a fast anomaly literature. Still, the sequence is instructive. The first wave asked whether a TeV electroweak multiplet with a few-hundred-keV splitting fits the event. This batch shifts to whether anything like that survives the Sun.

arXiv:2609.07807 — Not so good νs for Higgsino dark matter as LZ excess: stringent limits from Super-Kamiokande and IceCube (Debajit Bose et al.)

The authors compute solar capture of Higgsino DM through inelastic scattering on heavy solar nuclei, followed by annihilation to WW/ZZ. They confront the resulting neutrino flux with angular-cut atmospheric ν_e and ν_μ data from Super-K and IceCube. For the 1.08 TeV thermal Higgsino, splittings δ ≲ 557 keV are excluded, which covers the LZ-preferred 340–360 keV band. The strongest and weakest datasets differ by only ~20%. They also map limits for non-thermal Higgsino masses, where Super-K overtakes IceCube near 100 GeV.

The paper has drawn ~39 citations since 7 September. The most likely reason is that it is an independent cross-check of Pospelov–Ramani’s solar bound using different datasets and arriving at a comparable limit. That makes it the second half of the standard “solar capture disfavors Higgsinos” citation pair. The authors are candid that the thermal Higgsino survives if the local velocity distribution is non-standard, for example through LMC motion or streams. They also flag that the Helm form factor oscillates rapidly near 250 keV in xenon. An abstract-level note that one author thinks the event is background, sitting too close to the upper energy cut, may make the paper more memorable, but that is speculation.

arXiv:2609.06571 — The Inert Doublet Model of Dark Matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event (Lei Wang et al.)

This paper realizes the endothermic transition H N → A N through the off-diagonal Z coupling of the inert doublet. Because that coupling is fixed by electroweak strength, the scattering normalization is not a free parameter. The authors impose relic density, perturbativity, oblique parameters, elastic LZ limits and dwarf-galaxy limits. A profile likelihood on the event then gives a best fit at m_H = 1080 GeV and δ = 369 keV, with a GeV-scale charged splitting and λ_L ≈ −2×10⁻⁴. They stress that the event constrains δ far more tightly than the mass.

The ~35 citations likely come from its role as the canonical scalar counterpart to the Higgsino fit, with the full IDM constraint stack applied. The paper does not address solar capture, which is the main vulnerability of fixed-coupling interpretations. Lee–Youn (below) note that an inert-doublet fit lies in the same region as the Z₂-doublet case they estimate at roughly 10⁴ times the IceCube limit. The authors also acknowledge that the LZ likelihood cannot be fully reconstructed from public information.

arXiv:2609.07800 — Inelastic Singlet-Doublet Fermion Dark Matter in light of the 248 keV LZ event (Debasish Borah et al.)

Here a singlet-doublet fermion is split into pseudo-Dirac states by a hypercharge-1 scalar triplet, and the same triplet generates neutrino masses via type-II seesaw. The Majorana lightest state has no diagonal Z coupling, so the Z-mediated inelastic rate scales as sin⁴θ and the mixing sets the normalization. The preferred region moves with mixing: - At sinθ = 0.7, the fit prefers δ ~ 310–370 keV and masses of 10⁴–10^5.8 GeV. - At sinθ = 0.0135, it prefers δ ~ 30–180 keV and masses of 10^2.5–10^3.8 GeV.

Only the two small-mixing benchmarks evade elastic LZ bounds.

The ~34 citations likely reflect membership in the standard list of LZ interpretations. It also appears to be a direct precursor to the mixing-suppression mechanism developed in arXiv:2609.09138, which cites it. On substance it is thin: - The fit is a signal-only extended likelihood. - Relic density is taken from earlier work. - There is no solar or sideband analysis.

arXiv:2609.09138 — Mixing-suppressed inelastic dark matter: a minimal model for the LZ 248 keV event (Seung J. Lee et al.)

This is the most thorough of the four. The authors show that a full-strength Z transition at the recoil-inferred splitting predicts ~4000 events. Fixed-coupling models such as the Higgsino must therefore push δ deep into the halo tail, but solar gravitational acceleration undoes that suppression. A Majorana singlet mixed with a vector-like doublet instead suppresses the rate through sin⁴θ without shifting the spectrum. The same mixing drives capture as sin⁴θ and out-of-equilibrium annihilation as sin¹²θ, and weak Higgs cooling keeps the captured population extended.

With relic density and a one-event normalization imposed, they find δ = 302–305 keV conservatively (thermalized population). Under their cooling ansatz this rises to 331–343 keV near a 730–733 GeV endpoint. Falsifiable predictions include: - a tungsten rate ~46 times the xenon rate at the nominal ceiling; - no germanium or argon signal; - June-to-December rate ratios up to ~56.

Its ~34 citations are probably earned by its common-assumption comparison table, which places the Higgsino at ~4×10³ times the IceCube limit. That makes it a natural reference point for later papers.

item.title: Thursday, September 24, 2026
item.description:
No discoveries, one careful fit

After three days of experimental spectroscopy, today brings no new data. The most useful paper is a reanalysis. Woodward et al. arXiv:2609.26965 fit MiniBooNE and MicroBooNE jointly within 3+1 using simulation-based inference, with all data-driven factors removed. The preference for a sterile neutrino drops to 2.7σ, and the two experiments disagree with each other at ≥2.5σ inside the model. Elsewhere, the day’s cosmology papers find BBN deuterium constraining supercooled phase transitions, and the LZ papers now mostly work around solar capture rather than fit the event.

Themes

Sterile neutrinos under a sharper lens

Woodward et al. arXiv:2609.26965 also introduce an SBI method that makes trials-calibrated parameter-goodness-of-fit tension tractable. This continues last week’s statistics-tooling thread (coverage, ordering), here applied to a physics question. Around it: - Koranga et al. arXiv:2609.27540 trace δ₁₃ bias under PREM Earth profiles in 3+1. - Sengupta et al. arXiv:2609.27670 put visible-decay CP asymmetry on IBM hardware. - Chauhan et al. arXiv:2609.26908 propose the supernova 511 keV echo as an astrophysical “near detector” for pseudo-Dirac splittings.

Supercooling, baryons, and deuterium

This thread is new. Tanaka arXiv:2609.28348 finds that deuterium disfavors NANOGrav-compatible first-order transitions if the baryon asymmetry predates them. Girmohanta et al. arXiv:2609.27978 arrive at the same conclusion from the other side: in darkogenesis, dark-sector transport erases the inhomogeneity before it reaches visible baryons. Taken together, these papers make the timing of baryogenesis a gravitational-wave observable. Cervantes et al. arXiv:2609.27073 add a related effect, inverse phase transitions driven by chemical equilibration in freeze-in sectors.

LZ: designing around the Sun

Four papers today, and in three of them solar capture is the constraint being engineered around: - Girmohanta et al. arXiv:2609.28129 make the splitting density-dependent via an ultralight scalar, and admit to severe fine-tuning. - Tang et al. arXiv:2609.28415 go exothermic through a loop-generated dark photon. - Capolupo et al. arXiv:2609.28218 show that fermionic and scalar doublets matched in xenon produce distinct solar neutrino spectra.

The fourth, Maier et al., is covered in the picks below.

ML that fits in a trigger

Benyas et al. arXiv:2609.26899 distill the OmniLearned foundation model into a Deep Sets student, with the largest gains at low signal efficiency, where triggers operate. Cardini et al. arXiv:2609.28144 give a bit-exact INT8 GraphSAGE path to 53 ns on a VU13P. This follows the CMS L1 flow distillation from 09-15 and yesterday’s HL-LHC tracking cluster (see also D’Anzi arXiv:2609.28043).

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.26965: The most defensible MiniBooNE-vs-MicroBooNE comparison yet, reaching 2.7σ for 3+1 without asymptotic shortcuts.
  • arXiv:2609.28457: Drewes et al. run the first νMSM scan with complete quantum kinetics. The viable region is bounded on all sides and sits within SHiP and LHC reach.
  • arXiv:2609.28348: Tanaka shows BBN deuterium constraining supercooled-PT readings of NANOGrav. Baryogenesis timing becomes testable.
  • arXiv:2609.26870: Maier et al. argue that thermal electroweak multiplets fitting LZ sit beyond the HL-LHC. FCC-hh disappearing tracks and a 10–30 TeV muon collider are the program that can test them.
  • arXiv:2609.26888: Gruzinov et al. treat a Higgsed photon mass as environment-dependent, with Type I and Type II phases. Lab bounds may not apply in space.

From the community

arXiv:2609.28204 Study of the properties of sustainable materials for shielding against ionizing radiations — Faivre (physics.ins-det) finds that rammed earth needs about 20% more thickness than concrete for the same photon attenuation. This is a small, concrete data point for lower-carbon facility construction.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.27098 Anomalous soft photon production can be understood as photon emission during hadronisation — Völkl et al. (hep-ph) — isotropic emission during hadronisation reproduces the long-standing excess.
  • arXiv:2609.28223 Exclusive photoproduction of vector toponium within the color dipole picture — Goncalves et al. (hep-ph) — feasible in ultraperipheral pp only at FCC-hh; a footnote to the toponium thread.
  • arXiv:2609.27566 Exploring the short-range correlations in ¹⁶O+¹⁶O collisions at the LHC — Qi Liu et al. (nucl-th) — short-range correlations suppress central v₂{4}, so the oxygen runs double as a probe of the nuclear force.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.26965 — Tension between MiniBooNE and MicroBooNE within a 3+1 Sterile Neutrino Framework using Simulation-Based Inference (Julia P. Woodward (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) et al.)

With MiniBooNE’s f_π pion-flux correction removed, adding MicroBooNE BNB+NuMI data lowers the trials-calibrated 3+1 preference from ≥3.6σ (MiniBooNE alone) to 2.7σ. The two experiments sit in ≥2.5σ parameter-goodness-of-fit tension inside 3+1. The frequentist fit uses an SBI likelihood-ratio estimator (DNRE) with a normalizing-flow posterior (SNPE-C) to locate the best fit. The new ingredient is an SBI analogue of the Maltoni–Schwetz PG statistic, built from Δχ² differences relative to null. With it, 48,000 null trials become affordable.

The Wilks’ comparison shows why calibration matters. Without f_π, Wilks gives 7.1σ for MiniBooNE, 5.2σ for the joint fit, and 4.4σ tension. With f_π kept, the SBI joint preference drops to 1.8σ, but the tension rises to ≥3.2σ. In every f_π combination the BNB-only Wilks tension stays above 2σ, so the disagreement is not an artifact of inconsistent flux corrections.

Caveats: - Trial cap. 48k trials cap resolvable significance at ~4.25σ, so anything above 3.5σ is quoted as a lower bound. - Reconstructed NuMI prediction. MicroBooNE has released no event-level MC. The authors rebuilt the NuMI prediction from g4numi/PPFX/GENIE with a tuned approximate detector response (10-knot efficiencies per sample). Along the way they fixed a decay-at-rest flux bug worth up to 10% below 250 MeV. - Suspicious goodness of fit. MicroBooNE’s own χ²/dof of 86.62/179 is anomalously low. - Unexplained ν_μ excess. The low-energy ν_μ excess seen in both detectors is not understood, and the authors warn that quantitative comparisons should be read with care.

arXiv:2609.28457 — Sterile Neutrino Dark Matter Cries for GeV Heavy Neutral Leptons (Marco Drewes et al.)

This is the first νMSM scan using full quantum kinetic equations from baryogenesis through dark-matter production. The kinetics include chirality-flip effects, lepton-asymmetry back-reaction, and, decisively, the charge-odd (MSW-like) part of the HNL Hamiltonian. At the M₁ = 7 keV benchmark, the requirement to produce the QCD-epoch lepton asymmetry needed for Shi–Fuller conversion confines the HNL pair to a closed island.

Viable mass ranges: - Normal ordering (NO): the resonant-decay mechanism survives for 4 ≲ M ≲ 50 GeV. The 50 GeV upper bound is new. - Ignition mechanism (new): a self-amplifying MSW-driven instability that boosts μ_α by ~3 orders of magnitude, to |μ_α| ≃ 10⁻³. It reopens M < 5 GeV down to just above the kaon mass. - Inverted ordering (IO): only 0.8–7 GeV survives.

Experimental reach: - In the meson-accessible range, U² sits at least an order of magnitude above the seesaw floor. - SHiP covers the entire region below 2 GeV and much of 2–5 GeV. HL-LHC and Tera-Z machines cover the rest. - The predicted ΔM_phys adds a DM-specific test. For NO, HNL oscillation lengths can fall inside the SHiP decay volume; for IO, the pair looks Dirac-like.

Caveats: - A single DM mass is studied. - The scan uses momentum-averaged equations and neglects asymmetry depletion by N₁ production; both are checked only on the island boundaries. - Rates come from Fermi theory with free quarks, so the mass edges are uncertain below ~500 MeV and above ~50 GeV. - Structure-formation bounds on the computed spectra are deferred.

arXiv:2609.28348 — Big Bang Nucleosynthesis as a Probe of First-Order Phase Transitions (Masanori Tanaka)

Tanaka adds the reheating (α_n) dependence to BBN bounds on baryon inhomogeneity from supercooled transitions. The local reheating map is nonlinear, the spectral shape comes from the finite-bubble transition-time power spectrum, and proton/neutron diffusion is included. The result is imposed through the deuterium bound ε_BBN < 0.28 (1σ).

Results: - No bound exists for α_n < 0.1 with an optimistic k_cut = ∞, or for α_n < 0.5 with a conservative cut at the mean bubble separation. - For large α_n and 0.5 < T_n < 100 GeV, the disfavored region is β/H_n ≲ 5–6 (conservative) or ≲ 10–13 (optimistic). - Above ~10² GeV, diffusion weakens the bound.

NANOGrav: the NANOGrav-compatible region survives the conservative cut. It is largely disfavored only if the spectrum holds at sub-bubble scales, though much of it is still excluded keeping just modes with k < 2k_th. Evading the bound requires baryogenesis after reheating, or during the transition with baryon production tracking local entropy injection. That is the basis for the digest’s “baryogenesis timing” claim.

Caveats: - The result is 1σ only. - The baryon power spectrum is an admitted effective parametrization, and the bound is highly sensitive to the cutoff. - It assumes a pure exponential nucleation rate and energy release into the SM sector. - The paper is internally loose on bubble-wall baryogenesis. The abstract allows it if production tracks entropy, while Sec. 3 says the bound is “not evaded in general.” - A concurrent linearized analysis (Elahi et al.) finds β/H ≳ 10.3 α/(1+α), which Tanaka calls qualitatively consistent.

Full text was not supplied for the other two picks (Maier et al. arXiv:2609.26870, Gruzinov et al. arXiv:2609.26888), so no deep dives are given for them.

item.title: Wednesday, September 23, 2026
item.description:
LHCb’s light beauty-strange surprise

The day’s weight sits with the experiments, and specifically with spectroscopy. LHCb reports a new beauty-strange resonance at above 7σ arXiv:2609.25178 — unexpectedly light and narrow, “a substantial mass deficit” versus the quark model, billed as the first nonconventional single-beauty hadron. BESIII adds the heaviest light meson observed to date, the pseudoscalar η(2600) arXiv:2609.25158, and pins the Ω_b⁻ lifetime to twice the prior precision arXiv:2609.25370. This follows straight on from Sunday’s Ω_cc⁺ discovery — the experiments are filling in (and now breaking out of) the hadron spectrum at a steady clip. Underneath, the collider-QI program and the long-running LZ saga both keep moving, and a large instrumentation cluster lands.

Themes

Heavy-flavor spectroscopy

Three genuine experimental results plus a feasibility study. LHCb’s beauty-strange state arXiv:2609.25178 is the headline — a narrow width and mass deficit pointing to exotic dynamics in the open-beauty sector, where the charm-sector exotics have long lacked a counterpart. BESIII’s η(2600) arXiv:2609.25158 emerges from a model-independent partial-wave analysis of ΛΛ̅ in ψ(3686) radiative decays, alongside 0⁻⁺/0⁺⁺ threshold enhancements. The Ω_b⁻ lifetime arXiv:2609.25370 now agrees with heavy-quark-expansion predictions at improved precision. Dong et al. arXiv:2609.25870 project STCF sensitivity to the fully-charmed T_4c.

Collider quantum information

The entanglement-to-magic program the season tracked reaches its strongest form yet. Afik et al. arXiv:2609.25214 argue τ⁺τ⁻ from e⁺e⁻ at Belle II and FCC-ee can certify Nonlocal Advantage of Quantum Coherence — the strongest quantum correlation studied at colliders — with a single dedicated witness, and estimate the required precision (~1% at Belle II). Del Gratta et al. arXiv:2609.25217 supply the sober counterpoint: standard two-qutrit tomography of H→4ℓ can return a non-positive-semidefinite operator at NLO, though a robust concurrence lower bound survives. Two sides of the same maturing toolkit.

LZ, now an elastic form-factor story

The register shifted again. After Monday’s confining-sector readings, today’s crop explains the 248 keV recoil elastically, via composite form factors rather than inelastic splittings. Jung et al. arXiv:2609.25723 use a screened neutral four-dark-quark baryon whose charge form factor acts as a momentum band-pass filter; Khan et al. arXiv:2609.25114 use a toroidal electromagnetic moment through a dark photon. Delepine et al. arXiv:2609.26698 give a model-independent sideband analysis — a decisive 271–800 keV LZ search would test inelastic δ≳330 keV — and Gemmell et al. arXiv:2609.26570 tie an exothermic reading to the Galactic Center excess.

Instrumentation and tracking

A dense hardware/software day. Three CMS HL-LHC tracking papers converge on the heterogeneous mkFit+Patatrack+LST baseline, with LST’s new T4 quadruplet extending displaced-track acceptance to 60 cm arXiv:2609.26695, arXiv:2609.26383, arXiv:2609.26376. Multiple immersed-SiPM studies arXiv:2609.25532, arXiv:2609.25534, arXiv:2609.25093, White’s fast-timing review arXiv:2609.25358, and Parnassus cross-detector transfer learning from ALEPH to SLD arXiv:2609.25061.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.25178 — LHCb’s light, narrow beauty-strange state: >7σ, first nonconventional single-beauty hadron, a mass deficit versus the quark model. The discovery of the day.
  • arXiv:2609.25158 — BESIII’s η(2600), the heaviest light meson yet, from a clean model-independent PWA.
  • arXiv:2609.25214 — Afik et al.: NAQC in τ pairs, the strongest quantum correlation certifiable at a collider, with a one-observable witness for Belle II/FCC-ee.
  • arXiv:2609.25202 — Co et al. tie the CMB birefringence hint and the baryon asymmetry to a single rotating axion, with a falsifiable MeV-scale reheating prediction — direct progress on a standing open question.
  • arXiv:2609.25182 — Brambilla et al.: one open-quantum-system framework reproduces Υ suppression from Pb–Pb to O–O, supporting a common transport origin across system sizes.

From the community

De Swart arXiv:2609.25239 Before WIMPs: Neutrinos and the origins of particle dark matter — de Swart (physics.hist-ph) traces today’s particle-DM paradigm back to the short-lived neutrino-dominated universe of the early 1980s — a worthwhile reflection as WIMP confidence wanes.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.25153 Search for boosted W^±W^±H production — ATLAS Collaboration (hep-ex) — first direct handle on the quartic WWHH coupling; κ_WW constrained to -2.1–4.1.
  • arXiv:2609.26533 Compressed bino–wino in GmSUGRA — Khan et al. (hep-ph) — a high-scale realization of the ~20 GeV-splitting soft-lepton excess region, continuing the electroweakino thread.
  • arXiv:2609.26413 The Super-Composite Higgs — Agashe et al. (hep-ph) — SUSY plus compositeness, with an electron-EDM and squark-mass ceiling for FCC-hh.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.25178 — Discovery of an unexpectedly light and narrow beauty-strange state (LHCb collaboration et al.)

LHCb reconstructs B_s⁰π⁰ candidates in 9 fb⁻¹ of Run 1–2 data across three B_s⁰ channels (D_s⁻π⁺, J/ψϕ, D_s⁻π⁺π⁺π⁻), finding a narrow peak at a common mass in all three. A simultaneous fit yields 343⁺⁴⁴_-41 signal events at M=5698.9±1.5±0.6 MeV/c², with local (global) significance exceeding 8 (7)σ. The width is consistent with zero, Γ<9.8 (11.8) MeV at 90% (95%) CL. Interpreted as the 0⁺ scalar B_s0^(5700)⁰ — the beauty counterpart of D_s0^(2317)⁺ — its B_s⁰ splitting of 332.0 MeV/c² tracks the charm-sector 349.2 MeV/c², and sits well below quark-potential predictions, the same “mass deficit” seen in charm. This is billed as the first observation of a nonconventional single-beauty hadron, extending the exotic-dynamics pattern (chiral doubling, BK molecules, or compact tetraquarks) into the open-beauty frontier that had lacked a counterpart.

The main caveat is spin-parity ambiguity: the structure is equally compatible with the 1⁺ axial-vector partner decaying to B_s^*0(→B_s⁰γ)π⁰ with the photon unreconstructed (then M=5748.3 MeV/c²), or a superposition of both. Resolving the (0⁺,1⁺⁾ doublet requires the B_s⁰γ spectrum and awaits the larger post-2022 upgrade dataset. The state also enables the first data-driven 0⁺ pole for B_s⁰ heavy-to-light form factors, and predicts light narrow partners for Ω_cc⁺ and broad B-sector states.

arXiv:2609.25158 — Observation of η(2600) and Threshold Enhancements in the ΛΛ̄ System (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

Using 2712.4 million ψ(3686) events, BESIII performs a model-independent partial-wave analysis of ψ(3686)→γΛΛ̅, exploiting the self-analyzing weak decays of Λ/Λ̅ to extract spin correlations and cleanly separate 0⁻⁺ from 0⁺⁺. The near-threshold region (97.6% purity) is dominated by the ¹S_0 (0⁻⁺, 13.2σ) and ³P_0 (0⁺⁺, 5.4σ) waves, both showing strong threshold enhancements. In the ¹S_0 wave a new pseudoscalar η(2600) emerges at M=2625±26±6 MeV/c², Γ=140±58±46 MeV, significance 7.0σ — mass-consistent with the X(2600) seen in J/ψ→γπ⁺π⁻η’, and the heaviest light meson to date. Its production relative to η_c (12–22%) matches the X(2600)/η_c ratio (31%) in the other channel, supporting a common identity. The ³P_0 wave gives a 2262±34 MeV/c², 215±35 MeV state near f_0(2200).

The finding supports theoretical suggestions of a pseudoscalar glueball-like state near 2.6 GeV, and the η(ΛΛ̅) threshold enhancement invites hexaquark/baryonium interpretations (a predicted pseudoscalar ΛΛ̅ bound state at ~2.27 GeV/c²). Caveats: the η(2600) mass and width depend on lineshape choice (BW vs K-matrix), the η(ΛΛ̅) pole position is model-unstable (BW mass 2169 vs KM 1899 MeV/c²), and the dominant systematic on the ³P_0 branching fraction reaches −22.8% from additional-wave assumptions.

arXiv:2609.25214 — Nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence in tau-lepton pairs from electron–positron collisions (Yoav Afik et al.)

Afik et al. argue that e⁺e⁻→τ⁺τ⁻ is uniquely suited to certify Nonlocal Advantage of Quantum Coherence (NAQC) — the strongest collider quantum correlation studied — because, unlike top pairs at the LHC where NAQC survives only in unmeasurably thin phase-space slivers, tau pairs exhibit NAQC over broad angular windows. For unpolarized T-states with symmetric correlation matrix, they show NAQC reduces to ∑_i|C_i|>√(6) and construct a single-observable witness W_NA=∑_i|C_ii| (maximized in the diagonal basis), measurable via a pion opening-angle distribution D_i=Tr[P_i𝐂]/3, with D_i≥√(2/3) sufficient for NAQC. At Belle II (√(s)=10.58 GeV) NAQC peaks at ℭ^l_1_NA,max=2.59 within |cosΘ|<0.23, containing f_NAQC=0.18 of events; at the FCC-ee Z pole, 2.96 within 0.39, f=0.31. A 5σ observation needs ~1% precision at Belle II, a few percent at FCC-ee.

The result matures the collider-QI program from entanglement toward a certifiable NAQC hierarchy (NAQC⊂Bell⊂…), and includes the first proposed steering-game implementation in a collider — with asymmetric steering flagged as a future CP-violation probe. Caveats are honest: event counts and NAQC signal are anti-correlated (both peak/dip at cosΘ=0); estimates omit detector acceptance and reconstruction efficiencies; and the analysis is LO electroweak with an ultrarelativistic T-state approximation. The general proof that NAQC implies Bell nonlocality remains missing (numerical evidence only).

item.title: Tuesday, September 22, 2026
item.description:
Dark QCD claims the recoil

The LZ event is back at roughly a tenth of the listings — seven interpretation papers — but the register has shifted again: where September ran from fits to bounds to complementarity, today’s crop converges on composite readings, with confining dark sectors doing the work of the inelastic splitting. The day’s firmest single results sit elsewhere, though. Lin et al. arXiv:2609.22698 deliver a first-principles lattice value for the QCD contribution to the axion-photon coupling, resolving a standing ChPT discrepancy, and ATLAS arXiv:2609.24950 posts a null top-philic Z’ search that speaks directly to the year’s toponium-vs-scalar question. Underneath, the precision-QCD multiloop program from last week keeps rolling.

Themes

The LZ recoil, now a confining-sector story

The model zoo has a new organizing principle. Sannino et al. arXiv:2609.24988 read the 248 keV recoil as composite inelastic DM — a dimension-ten operator splitting the lightest baryon of an SU(3)_D theory, with a leptophobic baryon-number vector as mediator — while Sheng et al. arXiv:2609.23477 recast the inelasticity as a hyperfine transition within a single dark hadron in PQ-augmented dark QCD. Alongside: KK dark-photon mediation (Ahmed et al. arXiv:2609.22739), a SUSY-SU(6) pseudo-Dirac Higgsino arXiv:2609.23691, scalar-portal quark-Yukawa deviations (De arXiv:2609.23096), and cosmic-ray boosting (Chauhan et al. arXiv:2609.24982). The useful counterweight is Zurowski et al. arXiv:2609.24764, quantifying how shell-model form-factor uncertainties propagate into Si/Ge exclusion limits — the nuclear-structure caveat under all of this.

Precision QCD: form factors and DIS moments

The multiloop center of gravity from last week continues. Blümlein et al. arXiv:2609.24279 lay out the holonomic/large-moment machinery behind their gluonic three-loop massive form factors (companion to yesterday’s arXiv:2609.22034), Kidonakis arXiv:2609.23247 pushes the massive cusp anomalous dimension to four loops, and Pozzoli arXiv:2609.24910 reports the first leading-colour two-loop tt̅W amplitude. On the DIS side, Klann et al. arXiv:2609.23452 compute NLO heavy-quark coefficient Mellin moments and flag up to 20% errors in the standard quark-channel parametrisations.

Axions and dark photons, lab to lattice

A genuinely broad day. The standout is Lin et al. arXiv:2609.22698 pinning 𝒞_QCD=1.965(35) with domain-wall fermions — the strong-CP/axion lattice thread from August now reaching the photon coupling itself. On the search side, Durgut et al. arXiv:2609.22570 show CMS data parking/scouting can open the VBF ALP blind spot at 10 MeV–10 GeV; Liu et al. arXiv:2609.24085 constrain ultralight ALP birefringence with an FRB polarization array; and Debru et al. arXiv:2609.22638 tighten TRGB bounds on Higgs-portal scalars by two orders of magnitude via self-consistent MESA modelling.

Top-philic resonances

ATLAS arXiv:2609.24950 searches for a top-philic Z’ in same-sign/multilepton final states with a mass-parameterised transformer classifier, excluding m_Z’<1150 GeV for c_t=1 — a direct handle on the vector side of the toponium interpretation debate. Timed against it, Li et al. arXiv:2609.23576 find toponium production prospects at muon colliders and in Pb–Pb UPC unfavourable.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.22698 — Lin et al.: first-principles lattice axion-photon coupling, reconciling competing NLO ChPT results; a benchmark for every axion search.
  • arXiv:2609.24950 — ATLAS top-philic Z’ null to 1150 GeV; the vector-resonance constraint the toponium debate needed.
  • arXiv:2609.24988 — Sannino et al.’s dark-QCD composite reading of the LZ recoil; the cleanest of today’s confining-sector interpretations.
  • arXiv:2609.24279 — Blümlein et al.: the large-moment method behind the complete gluonic three-loop massive form factors, with analytic expansion around s=±∞ for the first time.
  • arXiv:2609.22555 — LHCb: first forward-rapidity measurement of W transverse helicity fractions out to y_W=5, agreeing with NLO.

From the community

Buss et al. arXiv:2609.24306 Jevons’ Paradox and Fast Generative Simulation for HEP — Buss et al. (hep-ex) warn that faster generative calorimeter simulation may raise total energy cost rather than lower it, and argue for realistic efficiency benchmarking — a computing-sustainability piece worth two minutes. And Benslama returns with arXiv:2609.23329 ARGUS — Benslama (physics.ins-det), a configuration-driven, experiment-agnostic detector-health monitoring framework, another concrete slice of collaboration plumbing.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.23367 LLM-Based FORM Code Generation with Verification-Driven Fine-Tuning — Chargeishvili (hep-ph) — an 8B fine-tune beats 756B frontier models on FORM after a verification-driven training corpus; FORM was a genuine zero-shot blind spot.
  • arXiv:2609.22930 The QCD Trace Anomaly in Pion Gravitational Form Factors — Corianò et al. (hep-ph) — the conformal anomaly dominates the TJJ correction to the pion trace form factor.
  • arXiv:2609.24237 Jet-like di-hadron correlations in pO, OO, and Ne–Ne — Prasad for ALICE (nucl-ex) — near-side widths in central OO approach Pb–Pb; the Run 3 light-ion program again.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.22698 — First-Principles Determination of the QCD Contribution to the Axion-Photon Coupling Using Domain-Wall Fermions (Tian Lin et al.)

Using two near-physical N_f=2+1 domain-wall ensembles (24D and 32Dfine, both M_π≈143 MeV), Lin et al. compute 𝒞_QCD — the model-independent QCD piece of g_aγγ — via anomalous Ward identities rather than direct topological-charge insertion. The trick is to split 𝒞_QCD into an exact anomaly term (5/3-ξ, fixed by charge assignments and z=m_u/m_d) plus a light-quark-mass-suppressed correction extracted from the isoscalar P⁰-VV three-point function, itself only a few percent of the total. Continuum extrapolation gives 𝒞_QCD^IS=1.619(30), 𝒞_QCD^IB=0.347(22), and 𝒞_QCD=1.965(35), with the IB shift dominated by the explicit -ξ term and a tiny pion-pole correction (-0.0059, 0.3%).

Why it matters: this is an independent lattice benchmark for the quantity entering every axion-photon search, in a regime where E/N and 𝒞_QCD partially cancel. Crucially, the authors resolve the standing NLO ChPT spread (1.63–2.05): the SU(3) result had a sign error (since corrected by its authors), and the U(3) IB discrepancy traces to an effective m_u/m_d ~15% too large. With common inputs, ChPT and lattice reconcile. Caveat: chiral fermions keep discretization mild, but only two lattice spacings enter the continuum limit; the extrapolated correction carries ~60% statistical uncertainty, and systematics are explicitly “not yet complete.” Their IS value sits 2.2σ from the competing gluonic background-field determination (𝒞_QCD^IS=1.47(6)), underscoring the value of independent systematics.

arXiv:2609.24950 — Search for a top-philic heavy resonance in association with top quarks (ATLAS Collaboration)

ATLAS searches for a colour-singlet top-philic Z’ decaying to tt̅ and produced via tt̅ Z’ or tZ’, using same-sign-dilepton and ≥3-lepton final states in 140 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV) plus 56 fb⁻¹ (13.6 TeV). A mass-parameterised transformer classifier (Salt framework), fed event- and object-level features including the Z’ mass hypothesis, discriminates signal from the dominant tt̅ tt̅ and tt̅ W/Z/H backgrounds; tt̅ W and non-prompt backgrounds are constrained in dedicated control regions. No excess is seen (largest local significance 2.4σ at m_Z’=400 GeV, c_t=3). For c_t=1, θ=0, masses below 1150 GeV are excluded (1250 expected); for c_t=3, below 2000 GeV (θ=0). Cross-section limits improve ~15× over the previous ATLAS single-lepton tt̅ Z’ search, which could not exclude c_t=1 at any mass.

Why it matters: this is the vector-resonance handle the toponium-vs-scalar debate around the low-mass tt̅ excess has lacked — a direct top-philic Z’ constraint, now reaching c_t=1. The (c_t²,θ) scans exploit the interplay of three-top (tZ’, ∝cos²θ) and four-top (tt̅ Z’) modes. Caveats: the result is statistics-dominated, with leading systematics from tt̅ tt̅ modelling; the SM four-top cross-section itself sits high versus theory (22.5⁺⁶.6_-5.5 vs 12.0±2.4 fb), and an alternative +70% tt̅ tt̅ fit leaves the limit unchanged only through competing normalisation/uncertainty effects.

arXiv:2609.24988 — Interpreting the LZ 248 keV Event using Dark QCD (Francesco Sannino et al.)

Sannino and Turner read LZ’s 248±23_stat±23_sys keV recoil candidate as composite inelastic dark matter. A confining SU(3)_D theory with SM-singlet dark quarks produces a Dirac baryon B∼UUD; a dimension-ten, dark-number-violating operator involving a U(1)B-breaking scalar S splits it into two Majorana states χ_1,2 with δ=m_2-m_1. Endothermic χ_1 N→χ_2 N scattering, mediated by a leptophobic baryon-number vector V, suppresses low-energy recoils. Their benchmark — m_1=1 TeV, δ=300 keV, M_V=1.44 TeV, g_B=0.146 (M_V/g_B≃9.9 TeV) — gives σ_p⁰⁼⁶.5×10⁻⁴³ cm², inside LZ’s two-sided 90% interval, yielding ~0.26 accepted events in 2.84 tonne-years. A 300 keV splitting maps to a matching scale Λ*≃12 TeV for order-one coefficients. The construction embeds anomaly-cancelling spectators, a stabilising ℤ_18 (forbidding proton decay), and pion/pseudoscalar decay channels.

Why it matters: it is today’s cleanest confining-sector reading of the LZ event, tying the inelastic splitting to explicit dark-QCD dynamics rather than a bolted-on mass gap, and it survives solar-neutrino (σ_p⁰<9.9×10⁻⁴³ cm² for bb̅) and ATLAS dijet (g_q⁹⁵≃0.084>0.05) bounds. Caveats are frank: the benchmark probes the high-speed halo tail near threshold (E_R^⋆=267 keV), so rates depend sensitively on the assumed velocity distribution and nuclear response near a diffraction minimum; the event is only 2.6σ post-look-elsewhere; the excited fraction must be f_2<10⁻³; and relic abundance is treated as input, not derived.

item.title: Monday, September 21, 2026
item.description:
R(D*) gets more precise, and a new baryon

The day’s weight sits with the flavor experiments. Belle II delivers its most precise hadronic-tag R(D⁽)) arXiv:2609.21947 — R(D^)=0.242±0.019±0.016, R(D)=0.439±0.055±0.046 — landing consistent with both the SM and prior measurements, which neither sharpens nor kills the LFU tension the memory has flagged all year as the flavor follow-up to watch. Alongside it, LHCb reports first observation of the doubly charmed Ω_cc⁺ at 8.7σ arXiv:2609.21921, a genuine discovery. The LZ recoil, meanwhile, is still generating theory but has shifted almost entirely into constraint-and-complementarity mode.

Themes

Heavy-flavor at the experiments

Belle II’s R(D⁽)) arXiv:2609.21947 is the headline: the R(D^) central value sits slightly below the SM, so if anything it eases rather than reinforces the anomaly — a notable data point against the August-through-September picture of a persistent tension surviving the consolidating null landscape. LHCb’s Ω_cc⁺ arXiv:2609.21921, mass 3725.9±1.0 MeV in Ω_c⁰π⁺, completes another rung of the doubly charmed spectrum. On the theory side, Guo et al. arXiv:2609.21464 trace the localized CP anomaly in B^±→K^±π⁺π⁻ to cross-channel K̅_0^*(1430)–ρ(770) interference — a direct descendant of August’s B→Kππ CP flare — and Iguro arXiv:2609.21253 dissects the baryon–meson sum rule in b→sνν̅.

LZ turns to constraints and complementarity

The recoil traffic persists but has fully migrated from fits to bounds. Bose et al. arXiv:2609.21823 reverse-engineer Wilson coefficients for LZ’s elastic operators and rule out weak-scale mass ranges via solar capture at IceCube/Super-K — the useful null. O’Hare arXiv:2609.21444 pins the June-16 lab-frame maximum DM speed to 792.7 km/s from IllustrisTNG/FIRE analogues, finding halo co-rotation does not rescue the high-velocity tail. Okada et al. arXiv:2609.21011 and Paul et al. arXiv:2609.22063 keep the inelastic-doublet reading alive via Z’-portal LHC complementarity and a type-II seesaw mass splitting, respectively.

Automated thermal cosmology

A distinct tooling cluster: Bouzoud et al. release AutoTherm arXiv:2609.20936, automating leading-order thermal production rates with model-independent Hard Thermal Loop resummation, and immediately apply it to gravitino/axino rates arXiv:2609.20937, flagging a factor ∼1.5–3 theory uncertainty that has been underappreciated. This is the season’s autodiff/automation ethos reaching thermal field theory.

Multiloop QCD and EFT theorems

Blümlein et al. arXiv:2609.22034 give analytic gluonic three-loop massive form factors across all four current types — continuing the precision-QCD center of gravity of the past week. Bresciani et al. arXiv:2609.20914 prove an all-order helicity-selection non-renormalization theorem for general EFTs, identifying new higher-loop zeros usable as checks on SMEFT calculations.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.21947 — Belle II’s most precise hadronic-tag R(D⁽*)); the central value nudges the LFU tension down, not up.
  • arXiv:2609.21921 — LHCb observes the doubly charmed Ω_cc⁺ at 8.7σ; a clean spectroscopy discovery.
  • arXiv:2609.21823 — Bose et al. rule out weak-scale elastic-operator LZ readings via solar capture; the day’s firmest constraint.
  • arXiv:2609.21464 — Guo et al. explain the localized B^±→K^±π⁺π⁻ CP anomaly through resonance interference — the August flare made mechanistic.
  • arXiv:2609.22034 — Blümlein et al.’s analytic three-loop massive form factors, gluonic sector complete.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.21104 Probing the Effective HZγ Coupling via Hγ Production at FCC-ee — Herrmann et al. (hep-ph) — a production-side handle resolving the sign ambiguity, 15% on HZγ.
  • arXiv:2609.21850 Search for pairs of dijet resonances with b jets — CMS (hep-ex) — mild 2.6σ at a 3.1 TeV four-jet mass; excludes RPV stops 0.5–0.8 TeV.
  • arXiv:2609.20949 Kinematic imbalance in ν_e interactions — MicroBooNE (hep-ex) — first such measurement, showing generator tensions away from FSI-dominated regions.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.21947 — Test of lepton flavor universality with B̅→D⁽)τν̅_τ and B̅→D⁽)ℓν̅_ℓ at Belle II (Belle II Collaboration et al.)

Using 387×10⁶ Υ(4S) decays with hadronic tagging, Belle II performs a simultaneous 2D fit in missing-mass-squared and residual calorimeter energy across five exclusive D⁽) samples, extracting R(D^)=0.242±0.019(stat)±0.016(syst) and R(D)=0.439±0.055±0.046 (correlations −0.40 stat, −0.20 syst). This supersedes the earlier hadronic-tag R(D^*) with twice the precision and delivers the first hadronic-tag R(D) at Belle II — the most precise hadronic-tagged determination to date, matching the best simultaneous measurements. Systematics are dominated by simulated-sample size (4.8%/8.4%) and, for R(D), B-tagging and low-momentum π⁰/γ efficiencies.

R(D^) sits within 0.5σ of the SM; R(D) is 2.0σ high, but the combination agrees with the SM at 1.5σ and with the world average at 1.3σ. The R(D^) central value landing below SM is the notable point for the LFU-anomaly narrative: this measurement neither sharpens nor kills the tension, easing rather than reinforcing it. Honest caveats are visible: the poorly-known gap-mode background is floated and found 42–82% smaller in data than simulation (validated against a B̅→D^π⁰ℓν control sample), and the hadronic-B normalization in the D^0_[D⁰π⁰] sample sits 3.1σ below prediction in the signal region — both absorbed into systematics rather than driving new uncertainty. The combined signal-plus-q²-sideband fit shifts the central values by only ~2%.

arXiv:2609.21921 — Observation of the doubly charmed baryon Ω_cc⁺ (LHCb collaboration et al.)

LHCb reports first observation of Ω_cc⁺ (scc) in Ω_c⁰π⁺, with Ω_c⁰→pK⁻K⁻π⁺, using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV data from the upgraded detector. A BDT-driven selection (32% signal efficiency, background retention 2.4×10⁻⁴) yields a peak at 8.7σ global significance (9.0σ local; 184±24 signal events), validated against the Ξ_cc⁺⁺→Ξ_c⁺π⁺ control channel (2770±110 events). The mass is 3725.9±1.0(stat)±0.2(syst)±0.4(lifetime)±0.6(ext) MeV/c², extracted via the mass difference M(Ω_cc⁺⁾⁻M(Ξ_cc⁺⁺⁾⁼¹⁰⁴.3 MeV/c² to cancel momentum-scale and companion-pion biases. The structure persists above 9σ with a >170 fs decay-time cut, consistent with a weakly decaying state and disfavoring a strong resonance.

This completes the SU(4)_f spin-½ 20-plet of ground-state baryons — every predicted member now established — and lands squarely in the 3660–3780 MeV/c² theory window, adding another rung to the doubly-charmed spectrum after this year’s Ξ_cc⁺ observation. The main caveat is intrinsic: the Ω_cc⁺ lifetime is unmeasured, so the selection-induced mass bias (parameterized linearly over 90–190 fs, correction 0.30 MeV/c² at the 140 fs midpoint) carries a dedicated 0.4 MeV/c² uncertainty. Lifetime and additional decay channels await the larger Run 3 dataset already in hand.

arXiv:2609.21823 — LZ’s Stairway to Heaνen: limits on elastic DM scatters from solar capture (Debajit Bose et al.)

Bose et al. take the elastic NREFT operators that LZ reported as ≥3σ fits to the 248 keV LZ230616 recoil and reverse-engineer their best-fit Wilson coefficients. Since LZ published favored regions only for ℒ_10^s (magnetic-dipole spin-spin) and the inelastic 𝒪_1^s, they build an approximate energy-dependent likelihood calibrated to reproduce LZ’s published local significances, validating against LZ’s own ℒ_10^s/𝒪_1^s curves (agreement to a factor of a few). They then compute solar capture rates (WimPyC) for each operator, assume equilibrium annihilation to {W⁺W⁻, bb̅, τ⁺τ⁻, νν̅}, and confront the resulting neutrino fluxes with IceCube (2016/2025 solar-direction ν_μ, 2014 atmospheric ν_e) and Super-K atmospheric data.

Large weak-scale mass ranges fitting LZ230616 are excluded, with the direct νν̅ channel giving the strongest and bb̅ the weakest limits; for ℒ_6^v, ℒ_8^s, ℒ_8^v the LZ-favored regions are almost entirely ruled out. This extends the “constraint-and-complementarity” mode the digest flags, mirroring the inelastic-operator treatment of Nguyen et al. Two honest caveats: the ℒ_4 operators survive even the νν̅ channel, and for several operators the excluded couplings lie where the EFT cutoff falls below the ~GeV solar-core momentum transfer — i.e., the NREFT description itself is invalid. Standard-halo velocities are assumed throughout, and LMC boosts or substructure could shift both the fits and the capture bounds.

item.title: Friday, September 18, 2026
item.description:
Structure again, and a direct Higgs width

The day’s weight sits where it has for three days running — nucleon structure and precision QCD — but the sharpest single result is elsewhere: ATLAS arXiv:2609.19948 sets a direct, coupling-independent bound Γ_H<307 MeV from on-shell H→γγ interference, a genuinely complementary handle to the off-shell method. Underneath, a large GPD/structure stack and a distinct cluster of statistical-inference infrastructure papers — the autodiff/tooling thread the memory has tracked all season, now surfacing as RooFit-AD, JAX interoperability, and HS3 serialization. LZ has thinned to a single follow-up. Collider BSM shows up as composite-Higgs resonance phenomenology rather than anomaly-chasing.

Themes

Nucleon structure and GPDs

A dense structure day anchored by two references: Guo et al.’s comprehensive GPD review arXiv:2609.19544, the first in two decades, and Su et al. arXiv:2609.20545, who show the large-momentum expansion can be relaxed near x=±ξ, opening the DA-like region to the lattice and recovering the expected partonic threshold kink for the first time. Around them: Melnitchouk’s higher-twist overview arXiv:2609.19620, Tezgin’s invertible Breit-frame/IMF map for spin-1 hadrons arXiv:2609.20714, a Drell-Yan angular-coefficient comparison favoring TMD at low Q_T arXiv:2609.20362, and a variational-quantum-circuit representation of pion FFs arXiv:2609.20557. This extends the four-loop/DIS center of gravity from the past two days.

The HEP statistics ecosystem

A coordinated cluster on statistical infrastructure. Galli arXiv:2609.19761 and the IRIS-HEP blueprint white paper arXiv:2609.19992 lay out the migration from RooFit/RooStats toward autodiff, JAX interoperability, and HS3; Fackeldey et al. arXiv:2609.19753 integrate CMS’s Combine into the PyHEP ecosystem via the Analysis Grand Challenge. The conceptual standout is Dorigo arXiv:2609.20007, who shows a covariance matrix can change not just a fit but the likelihood-ratio ordering — ~7.6% of experiments flip their confidence decision even under exact calibration. This is the tooling wave from August maturing into the statistics layer.

Composite-Higgs resonances and portals

Collider BSM today is model-building, not excess-fitting. Kunkel arXiv:2609.19918 and Caliri arXiv:2609.19919 work the exotic spectrum of gauge-fermionic composite Higgs — colour-sextet baryons (≲2.64 TeV) and spin-1 resonances down to 1.5 TeV. Detering et al. arXiv:2609.19258 show HL-LHC + FCC-ee + FCC-hh can in principle distinguish marginal from higher-dimensional Higgs portals above threshold, and Dey et al. arXiv:2609.19305 contrast SUSY and compositeness benchmarks in resonant bb̅ττ di-Higgs. The EFT-and-future-collider framing runs throughout.

Hadron spectroscopy converging

Several independent handles on the same states. BESIII observes double-ss̅ production at 40% of the inclusive ϕ rate arXiv:2609.20154, in line with the double-cc̅ surprise and a challenge to hadronization theory. Molecular readings recur — P_c pentaquarks arXiv:2609.19749, Ω(2012) line shapes arXiv:2609.20654 — while Peng et al. arXiv:2609.19673 argue the ψ(4160) mass shift is a coherent-interference artifact, not a real shift.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.19948 — ATLAS’s direct Γ_H<307 MeV from H→γγ interference; no coupling assumptions, complementary to off-shell bounds.
  • arXiv:2609.20545 — Su et al. extend lattice GPD computability into the x∼±ξ region and see the threshold kink for the first time.
  • arXiv:2609.20154 — BESIII’s double-ss̅ observation; a clean hadronization number that echoes the double-charm puzzle.
  • arXiv:2609.20007 — Dorigo: coverage is not ordering. A foundational warning about covariance-as-model, with a concrete failure rate.

From the community

Benslama arXiv:2609.19658 Proposing, never assigning: fair allocation of control-room shifts — Benslama (physics.ins-det) formalizes shift scheduling as ranked-wish allocation under institutional quotas, with an independent rule-checker — a rare, concrete piece of collaboration plumbing. And the IRIS-HEP statistical blueprint arXiv:2609.19992 — Feickert et al. (hep-ex) sets the community’s inference-tooling agenda through 2026.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.20448 A comprehensive theory framework for δ_C in superallowed beta decays — Seng (nucl-th) — argues the standard isospin-breaking split violates nucleon-basis independence, bearing on |V_ud| and Cabibbo unitarity.
  • arXiv:2609.20500 Particle Physics Driven by Quantum Technology — Bloch et al. (hep-ph) — a review of quantum simulation and sensing for BSM searches.
  • arXiv:2609.20135 Heterogeneous vectorized tracking for the HL-LHC — Vourliotis for CMS (hep-ex) — the Phase-2 GPU+CPU tracking baseline.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.19948 — Constraints on the Higgs boson total width from on-shell signal–background interference in H→γγ (ATLAS Collaboration)

ATLAS extracts a direct, coupling-independent bound on Γ_H from the interference between the resonant gg→H→γγ amplitude and the continuum diphoton background, which distorts the m_γγ lineshape — an antisymmetric peak shift (~-70 MeV at the SM width) plus a ~-1.7% yield reduction, both scaling as √(μ Γ_H/Γ_H^SM). Using the full 140 fb⁻¹ Run 2 dataset in two p_T^γγ categories, with m_H externally constrained from H→ZZ^*→4ℓ and μ profiled, they set an observed (expected) 95% CL limit Γ_H<307 (258) MeV, ~75× the SM value; the best fit is Γ̂H=13⁺⁷⁵-13 MeV and μ=1.08±0.12. Statistics-only, the limit tightens to 105 (87) MeV.

Why it matters: unlike the off-shell ZZ/WW method (ATLAS combined Γ_H=3.6⁺².1_-1.6 MeV), this probe makes no assumption that on- and off-shell couplings coincide, so it remains valid under exotic or invisible decays — a genuinely orthogonal handle even at ~30× weaker sensitivity. The caveat is explicit and dominant: the measurement is systematics-limited, with the largest single contribution (49 MeV at 68% CL) from the 39% theory uncertainty on the gg-interference K-factor (K_I=1.64, NLO→NNLOsv), followed by the m_H constraint (43 MeV). Because interference scales as √(Γ_H), the K_I uncertainty dominates entirely near the limit. The authors flag that interference calculations matched to parton showers are the needed improvement, and note only two p_T^γγ bins are justified given current modelling.

arXiv:2609.20545 — Computability of GPDs near x=±ξ in Lattice QCD (Yushan Su et al.)

Su, Ji, Liu, and Zhang argue that the LaMET large-momentum expansion for GPDs does not require the naive EFT condition 2|x±ξ|P^z≫Λ_QCD near the transition points x=±ξ, where one parton momentum vanishes. Their argument parallels DVCS factorization: soft contributions associated with the vanishing scale are power-suppressed, just as photon-DA physics enters DVCS only at O(Λ_QCD²/Q²⁾. The condition reduces to keeping at least one hard scale, 2(|x|+|ξ|)P^z≫Λ_QCD, dramatically enlarging the computable window that would otherwise exclude bands of width ~0.4 around x=±ξ for realistic P^z∼2–3 GeV.

Reanalyzing four existing nonzero-skewness datasets (ETMC20/21/25, MSULat23) with complete one-loop matching and a carefully ordered regulator hierarchy (ϵ_2≪|ϵ_1|→0, the only convergent ordering), they recover GPDs that are continuous at x=±ξ but with discontinuous derivatives — the expected partonic threshold kink from soft-quark zero modes, seen on the lattice for the first time and consistent with polynomiality-preserving GPD models. The previously reported discontinuities are attributed to regulator artifacts in the matching. This yields the first first-principles prediction of GPDs in the distribution-amplitude-like region (|x|<ξ), smoothly connecting quark and antiquark PDF-like regimes — directly relevant to DVCS extractions and the GUMP global-analysis program.

Caveats: the result rests on one-loop matching applied to existing data at coarse pion masses (mostly 260 MeV) and modest momenta, and the region remains uncomputable when both x and ξ are small (near x=0) or near the endpoints x=±1.

arXiv:2609.20154 — Observation of double ss̅ production in e⁺e⁻ collision at √(s)=3.08 GeV (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

BESIII reports the first systematic observation of double-ss̅ production in the e⁺e⁻ continuum, tagging a prompt ϕ recoiling against a second strangeness-carrying system X(ss̅) ∈{η,η’,K⁺K⁻,K⁺K^-,K⁻K^+,K⁰K̅⁰,K⁰K̅^0}. From 167 pb⁻¹, they measure σ(e⁺e⁻→ϕ+anything)=506.3±6.9±19.7 pb (a first) plus the individual ϕ+X(ss̅) cross sections, with ϕK⁺K^-, ϕK⁻K^+, ϕK⁰K̅⁰, ϕK⁰K̅^0 reported for the first time. After subtracting ISR (ϕγ_ISR) to isolate the QCD-driven part, the ratio is R_ss̅=(40.4±1.7_stat±1.5_syst)%.

Why it matters: this large ratio directly echoes the double-cc̅ surprise seen by Belle and BABAR at 10.6 GeV, where R_cc̅ exceeded early NRQCD predictions and drove years of theory refinement. Extending the phenomenon to the strange sector — in the deep non-perturbative regime — supplies a clean hadronization number that challenges the frameworks tuned to R_cc̅ and opens a window on possible flavor correlations in fragmentation. The synergy of strange and charm “flavor portals” is the framing.

Caveat, stated by the authors: the measurement omits higher-multiplicity final states (e.g. ϕK⁺K⁻π⁰), so R_ss̅ is a lower bound on total double-ss̅ rate; f_ss̅ assumptions for η/η’ and f-states carry model dependence, and several sub-channels have 6–11% systematics dominated by efficiency and background modelling.

Citation radar

This week’s radar is dominated by a single experimental spark: LUX-ZEPLIN’s report of one anomalous ~248 keV nuclear-recoil event (LZ230616), with a 3.4σ local / 2.6σ global significance. All five heavily-cited papers below are theory responses posted within days of the LZ preprint, and together they map the interpretive landscape that has formed almost overnight—endothermic vs. exothermic vs. neutrino-upscattering, Higgsino vs. inert-doublet vs. axion-portal. The rapid, cross-citing cluster (these papers reference each other extensively) is itself the story: a genuine community pile-on around a possible first direct-detection signal, with everyone racing to stake a mechanism and stress-test it against solar-capture and halo-tail constraints.

arXiv:2609.04186 — Axion Portal Dark Matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event (James Unwin)

Unwin proposes an elastic explanation of the LZ event, in deliberate contrast to the inelastic Higgsino interpretations dominating the early literature. The paper UV-completes the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar operator ℒ₄ = (χ̄iγ⁵χ)(N̄iγ⁵N)—one of the templates for which LZ reported its largest local significances—via an axion portal: Dirac fermion dark matter (m_χ ≈ 400 GeV) coupled to a GeV-scale pNGB mediator, with a single multi-TeV vectorlike quark completing the up-quark coupling. The hard recoil spectrum arises from momentum dependence (moderated by a pion pole) rather than inelastic kinematics, so it is insensitive to the uncertain high-velocity halo tail; the model reproduces the relic abundance via p-wave freeze-out and brackets the LZ significance at 2.6–3.2σ.

At ~43 citations since early September, its pull likely comes from being the first full elastic UV completion of a favored LZ operator—offering a distinct, halo-robust alternative just as the field worried the Higgsino reading was fragile. The bonus correlation with the first-row CKM unitarity deficit adds cross-sector appeal.

arXiv:2609.04163 — TeV Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ High-Recoil Event with Intermediate-Scale Electroweak Gauginos (Xiaokang Du et al.)

Du and Wang address a specific tension in the popular TeV-Higgsino reading: reproducing a sub-MeV neutral-Higgsino splitting normally pushes electroweak-gaugino masses toward ~10⁷ GeV. They show that with opposite-sign bino and wino masses, the non-universal SU(5) GUT boundary condition M₁ᴳ/M₂ᴳ = −3/5 cancels the leading dimension-five contribution, and homogeneous one-loop running preserves this down to the Higgsino scale. The residual finite-gaugino terms then yield a controlled branch with a wino near 120 TeV for a 350 keV gap, μ = 1.091 TeV, tanβ = 10. They classify the mixed SU(5) representations (1+24, 1+75, 1+200) that realize the ratio, but candidly note the small gap is far more sensitive to bino–wino alignment than to overall scale, and that the inelastic Z coupling remains unsuppressed—so the full-density thermal Higgsino stays in tension with solar-capture bounds.

The ~42 citations reflect its role as the top-down SUSY-model-building companion to the phenomenological Higgsino fits: it supplies a concrete GUT-scale mechanism others can cite when invoking small Higgsino splittings.

arXiv:2609.04185 — Atmospheric neutrino up-scattering explanation of LZ 2026 excess (Sk Jeesun et al.)

Jeesun and Majumdar break from the dark-matter framing entirely: they explain the isolated high-recoil event via atmospheric neutrinos up-scattering into a massive BSM fermion χ (ν𝒩→χ𝒩) through a scalar mediator. The key kinematic feature is that producing a ~GeV-mass χ requires a minimum recoil energy of ~200 keV, naturally cutting off the low-energy tail and mimicking an isolated event exactly where LZ sees one. They identify a closed 90% CL band—m_χ ≈ 0.7–2 GeV, coupling √(y_χy_q)/m_φ ≈ 2×10⁻² GeV⁻¹—bounded below by the low-recoil veto and above by the falling atmospheric flux, and argue collider/beam-dump/supernova limits evade this region.

At ~40 citations, this is the field’s principal non-dark-matter alternative, keeping the interpretation space honest. Its value is providing a distinct testable hypothesis (a sterile-neutrino-like signal) that upcoming low-background experiments could distinguish from the halo-DM readings.

arXiv:2609.02505 — Dark Matter as the Z₂ Partner of the Standard Model Higgs Boson (Yasunori Nomura)

Nomura connects the LZ event to an inert-doublet model previously selected—in prior work—to fit a Fermi-LAT Galactic-halo gamma-ray excess at several-hundred-GeV mass. The conceptual hook is that the inert Z₂ parity is exactly equivalent (by field redefinition) to an interchange symmetry between two Higgs doublets, making dark matter the Z₂-odd partner of the SM Higgs. Phenomenologically, gauge invariance fixes the off-diagonal Z coupling, and the halo-plus-thermal mass window (440–600 GeV) selects a narrow strip of ~350 keV neutral splittings near the kinematic boundary where inelastic Z-exchange can produce the recoil. A sharp prediction follows: because scattering probes the extreme halo tail, future events should show large annual modulation peaking near early summer—and LZ230616 occurred June 16.

The ~32 citations track the paper’s ambition to unify two anomalies (gamma-ray excess + LZ event) under one minimal, technically-natural model. The v2 note honestly concedes the solar-capture (Pospelov–Ramani) constraint may require δ ≳ 500 keV, showing the interpretation under active pressure.

arXiv:2609.05204 — Exothermic Dark Matter at LZ (Carlos Henrique de Lima)

de Lima pursues the exothermic route: a metastable excited state χ_H down-scatters (χ_H𝒩→χ_L𝒩), releasing the mass splitting δ into the recoil so the signal does not require the halo’s high-velocity tail—the chief liability of endothermic Higgsino readings. Realized in a minimal inelastic dark-photon model, the fit favors m_χ ~ 30–200 GeV and δ ~ 0.5–1 MeV (bounded by δ < 2m_e for cosmological stability), with GeV-scale mediators and ε ~ 10⁻⁶. Both secluded freeze-out (yielding a small excited fraction f_H) and low-reheating freeze-in can supply the rate. The standout prediction is target dependence: because xenon is being probed near its diffraction minimum, argon and germanium should see ~3× more events at higher recoil energies (Table 1), giving DEAP-3600 and DarkSide-20k a clean cross-check.

At ~31 citations, its appeal is offering the halo-robust, testable counterpoint to endothermic models—and explicitly evading the solar-capture bound because χ_L is kinematically inert. Its dense cross-referencing of the whole LZ-interpretation cluster makes it a natural hub in this fast-moving conversation.

item.title: Thursday, September 17, 2026
item.description:
The 17 MeV boson meets cosmic muons

The day’s sharpest single paper is a debunking: Benmansour et al. arXiv:2609.18383 show that Geant4 simulations of cosmic-ray muon coincidences in the Atomki five- and six-arm spectrometers reproduce the very opening-angle peaks — near 140° in the ⁸Be window, 120° in the ⁴He window — long read as evidence for a 17 MeV boson, with a cosmic-to-signal ratio above unity. It doesn’t close the case, but it puts the burden squarely back on the beam-off studies. Around it the weight sits where it did yesterday, in precision QCD and nucleon structure, plus a genuine f0(980) convergence and a quiet continuation of the LZ story — now down to three papers, all cosmological escape routes rather than fits.

Themes

Precision QCD and structure

A dense fixed-order/structure day. Gauld et al. arXiv:2609.17812 deliver bottom-flavoured jets through bb̅ production at NNLO+PS with full mass effects, confronting ATLAS/CMS/LHCb and pinning the jet-algorithm differences to g→bb̅ splittings. Chen et al. arXiv:2609.18828 complete the NLO electroweak corrections to gg→γγ — sub-percent inclusive but −10% in the tails, with a dip-bump at the Higgs threshold. On the formal side, Skands arXiv:2609.18102 proposes “Cat’s Cradle” diagrams as an intermediate power counting for resolved jet substructure, Rainaldi arXiv:2609.18627 recasts DGLAP scheme transformations as a gauge group, and Prygarin et al. arXiv:2609.18269 give a Lévy-process reading of the forward BFKL kernel. This extends yesterday’s four-loop/splitting-function center of gravity.

The f0(980) under a microscope

Three independent angles on the same scalar, a day after BESIII’s D_s→f_0(980) favored an ss̅-dominant picture. Kumano arXiv:2609.17974 argues from Belle fragmentation functions that f0(980) looks like qq̅ (ss̅) at high energy even if it is KK̅-molecular at low energy — structure that depends on the probing scale. Lacey arXiv:2609.17765 reaches a compatible conclusion via anisotropy-response scaling in p+Pb, finding a single-meson-like response distinct from the molecular benchmark. Zheng et al. arXiv:2609.18890 work the heavier f0(1500) in rare B_s decays. A rare case of low- and high-energy methods triangulating one state.

LZ evasion goes cosmological

The recoil traffic is a trickle, and the surviving papers all target the IceCube/solar-capture bound. Nagata et al. arXiv:2609.18564 set the relic abundance by a primordial asymmetry rather than freeze-out, so there is no antiparticle population to annihilate in the Sun — the cleanest structural escape yet. Xing arXiv:2609.17935 produces the excited state by galactic self-scattering and detects it exothermically; Ge et al. arXiv:2609.16529 supply relativistic inelastic Xe response functions that could shift any of these fits. The falsifiability pivot the memory tracked has fully given way to model cosmology.

ML in event reconstruction

The tooling wave keeps colonizing reconstruction. Mao et al. arXiv:2609.18928 introduce VyPER, a hypergraph-plus-diffusion framework doing jet assignment and neutrino kinematics jointly; Lazarovits et al. arXiv:2609.16276 offer PSICHE, probabilistic clustering with learned variable jet sizes in space and time. Two Tsoi et al. papers push self-supervised pre-training — VICReg-based mass regression arXiv:2609.17726 and augmentation-free EMD pairing arXiv:2609.17738 — and Benne et al. arXiv:2609.17659 use domain adaptation to kill background sculpting in weakly-supervised anomaly searches.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.18383 — Benmansour et al.: cosmic muons reproduce the Atomki opening-angle peaks at cosmic-to-signal ratio above unity; the strongest challenge yet to the 17 MeV boson.
  • arXiv:2609.18564 — Nagata et al.: asymmetric inelastic DM removes the IceCube constraint by construction, the cleanest LZ escape route.
  • arXiv:2609.17812 — Gauld et al.: b-jets at NNLO+PS with full mass effects, resolving jet-flavour-algorithm differences against LHC data.
  • arXiv:2609.17974 — Kumano: f0(980) looks ss̅ at high energy, molecular at low — scale-dependent hadron structure, testable in fragmentation.
  • arXiv:2609.18892 — Du et al.: transverse tau spin correlations gain a factor of ~26 on the weak EDM at FCC-ee/CEPC, three orders beyond ALEPH.

From the community

The ESPPU Electroweak WG documents its collider-comparison assumptions and theory-uncertainty treatment for the 2026 Physics Briefing Book (de Blas et al. arXiv:2609.18607) — the reproducibility backbone behind the future-collider SMEFT fits. And Cabrera et al. arXiv:2609.18799 After 60 years, here comes the Sun argue that reactor-pinned oscillation parameters finally let solar neutrinos probe the Sun itself, if the field builds detectors that can breach the ¹⁴C wall on the pp flux.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.18906 New Dynamics (?) of J/ψJ/ψ and ΥΥ families from QCD Laplace sum rules — Narison (hep-ph) — reads X(6600) as a molecule ground state and X(6900)/X(7100) as radial mixtures.
  • arXiv:2609.17952 D⁽)Δ interactions and the molecular Σ_c(3200)⁰* — Rui Chen et al. (hep-ph) — a one-boson-exchange molecular reading of LHCb’s new charmed baryon, with predicted partners.

Paper arXiv:2609.17974

Title: Structure of Λ(1405) and f_0(980) shown in fragmentation functions

FULL TEXT (from arXiv HTML rendering): Structure of Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) and f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) shown in fragmentation functions

S. Kumano

Email: shunzo.kumano@ozyegin.edu.tr

Affiliation: Department of Natural and Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of Engineering, Özyeğin University, Çekmeköy, Istanbul 34794, Türkiye

Affiliation: KEK Theory Center, Institute of Particle and Nuclear Studies, KEK, and J-PARC Branch, KEK Theory Center, Institute of Particle and Nuclear Studies, KEK, 203-1, Shirakata, Tokai, Ibaraki, 319-1106, Japan

September 16, 2026

Abstract

The internal quark-gluon configuration of the exotic hadron candidates Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) and f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) is investigated by using their fragmentation functions. Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) is one of the most probable candidates for an exotic hadron with an internal structure of a meson-baryon molecule or a five-quark state, and f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) could be a tetraquark, a K ​ K ¯ K\bar{K} molecule, or an ordinary quark-antiquark meson. There were experimental indications that the second moment of the Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) fragmentation function has an anomalously small value in comparison with the ordinary hadrons from the electron-positron annihilation measurements. We explain this fact by the meson-baryon molecular configuration or the compact five-quark state, and this proposal opened a field of exotic-hadron studies by the fragmentation functions. The details of these fragmentation-function studies are explained in this proceedings for Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) , together with the studies of f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) . These fragmentation functions can be measured at various facilities in the near future including the LHC, Belle II, EIC, and EicC, so that the internal structure of these particles will be clarified.

1 Introduction

Hadron mass is one of the fundamental quantities in physics; however, it has not been understood yet at the level of elementary particle physics [ 1 , 2 ] . There are two mass systems in our universe. One is the Higgs mass system for quarks and leptons, and the other is the hadron mass system for protons, neutrons, and other hadrons. The Higgs mechanism explains only a few percent of the nucleon mass, and the remaining part comes from the strong interaction. Currently, the origin of hadron masses is understood by the trace anomaly of the energy-momentum tensor and the quark condensate [ 1 , 2 ] . However, this explanation is not complete, so that the origins of hadron masses and hadron spins are the topics of current investigations both theoretically and experimentally [ 3 ] . In particular, the internal structure of exotic hadron candidates, such as Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) and f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) , is one of the most interesting topics because their structure cannot be explained by the ordinary quark model.

The fragmentation function indicates a probability of finding a hadron from a parton (quark or gluon), and it is expressed by the variable z z , which is the energy fraction of the hadron from the parton. The fragmentation functions are used generally for explaining hadron-production cross sections in high-energy reactions, and they are also valuable for finding the internal structure of exotic hadron candidates. In this proceedings, the internal structure of Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) and f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) is investigated by using their fragmentation functions.

2 Determination of fragmentation functions

The fragmentation functions are determined from the experimental data of hadron-production cross sections, mainly by the electron-positron annihilation processes e + ​ e − → h ​ X e^{+}e^{-}\to hX . The fragmentation functions are then obtained by the global analysis of these experimental data, in the same way used for determining the parton distribution functions.

The fragmentation function is expressed by two terms, one is the singlet fragmentation function D S D_{S} and the other is the non-singlet fragmentation function D N ​ S D_{NS} , in terms of the flavor-singlet and non-singlet distributions. Here, the singlet and non-singlet fragmentation functions are given by the quark and antiquark fragmentation functions.

The z z dependence of the fragmentation function is generally parametrized by the following form at the initial scale Q 0 2 Q_{0}^{2} :

D i h ​ ( z , Q 0 2 ) = N i ​ z α i ​ ( 1 − z ) β i , \displaystyle D_{i}^{h}(z,Q_{0}^{2})=N_{i}\,z^{\alpha_{i}}(1-z)^{\beta_{i}},

(1)

where N i N_{i} is the normalization constant, and α i \alpha_{i} and β i \beta_{i} are the parameters to be determined by the experimental data. The subscript i i indicates the quark flavor or gluon. The fragmentation functions are evolved from the initial scale Q 0 2 Q_{0}^{2} to the experimental scale Q 2 Q^{2} by the DGLAP evolution equations [ 4 ] .

The second moment of the fragmentation function is defined by

⟨ z ⟩ = ∫ 0 1 𝑑 z ​ z ​ D ​ ( z ) ∫ 0 1 𝑑 z ​ D ​ ( z ) . \displaystyle\langle z\rangle=\frac{\int_{0}^{1}dz\,z\,D(z)}{\int_{0}^{1}dz\,D(z)}.

(2)

This quantity indicates the average energy fraction of the hadron from the parton. The second moment is a useful quantity for investigating the internal structure of hadrons.

3 Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) and f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980)

The Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) is a hyperon with spin-parity J P = 1 / 2 − J^{P}=1/2^{-} , and it is one of the most probable candidates for an exotic hadron. The Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) is considered to be a meson-baryon molecular state of N ​ K ¯ N\bar{K} or a compact five-quark state. The internal structure of Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) is investigated by using the fragmentation functions.

The fragmentation function of Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) was determined from the electron-positron annihilation data. There were experimental indications that the second moment of the Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) fragmentation function has an anomalously small value in comparison with the ordinary hadrons [ 5 ] . This fact is explained by the meson-baryon molecular configuration or the compact five-quark state.

The f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) is a scalar meson with spin-parity J P = 0 + J^{P}=0^{+} . The internal structure of f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) is not well understood, and it is considered to be a tetraquark, a K ​ K ¯ K\bar{K} molecule, or an ordinary quark-antiquark meson. The internal structure of f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) is investigated by using the fragmentation functions.

The fragmentation functions of f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) were determined from the Belle experimental data [ 6 ] . The second moment of the f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) fragmentation function was obtained, and the internal structure of f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) is discussed.

4 Summary

The internal structure of exotic hadron candidates Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) and f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) was investigated by using their fragmentation functions. The second moment of the Λ ​ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) fragmentation function has an anomalously small value in comparison with the ordinary hadrons, and this fact is explained by the meson-baryon molecular configuration or the compact five-quark state. The internal structure of f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) is also investigated by using the fragmentation functions.

These fragmentation functions can be measured at various facilities in the near future including the LHC, Belle II, EIC, and EicC, so that the internal structure of these particles will be clarified.

Paper arXiv:2609.18892

Title: Probing tau weak dipole couplings via transverse spin correlations at the CEPC/FCC-ee

FULL TEXT (from arXiv HTML rendering): Only the abstract was available for this paper.

Abstract: We propose a novel strategy to probe the tau weak dipole couplings—the weak anomalous magnetic dipole moment a τ W a_{\tau}^{W} and the weak electric dipole moment d τ W d_{\tau}^{W} —via transverse spin correlations in e + e − → Z → τ + τ − e^{+}e^{-}\to Z\to\tau^{+}\tau^{-} at future lepton colliders. Focusing on the transverse and normal polarization components, we construct dedicated asymmetry observables that isolate the dipole-induced effects with enhanced sensitivity. Using semileptonic tau-decay channels, we show that the transverse spin correlations offer markedly improved precision, with the achievable sensitivity reaching the level of ∼ 10 − 4 \sim 10^{-4} for a τ W a_{\tau}^{W} and ∼ 10 − 20

e ​

cm \sim 10^{-20}\,e\,\text{cm} for the CP-violating d τ W d_{\tau}^{W} at the CEPC/FCC-ee. This corresponds to nearly three orders of magnitude improvement over existing ALEPH limits, providing a powerful and complementary probe of new physics in the tau sector.
